title: X は Y です (X is Y / Topic & Copula)
meaning: Identify or describe a topic: as for X, it is Y.
connection: X は noun です; noun です is enough when the topic is understood.
nuance: は is written は but pronounced わ when it marks the topic. It tells the listener what the statement is about; it is not simply a replacement for the English subject. If both speakers already know the topic, omit it: 学生です can mean I am a student, she is a student, or they are students, depending on context. Japanese nouns generally do not require a/an and do not automatically change for plural number. です makes the noun predicate polite and non-past; it does not change with person or number. Do not append です to an ordinary finite verb such as 行くです. Adjectives have their own patterns, introduced later: 静かです and 高いです, but not 静かだです or 高いだです. Use a name/title rather than repeatedly translating English you as あなた.
keyTakeaway: State the topic only when needed; put the identifying noun before polite です.

sentences.japanese: 私はアリゾナ大学の学生です。
sentences.english: I am a student at the University of Arizona.
sentences.literal: I topic University-of-Arizona's student am.
sentences.nuanceNote: Standard polite self-identification.

quiz.question: スミスさん（　　）イギリス人です。
quiz.translation: Smith-san is British.
quiz.grammarFocus: Topic particle は
quiz.ruleHint: X は noun です; noun です is enough when the topic is understood.

explanations.reason: Correct! は marks Smith-san as the topic being identified as British.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects of action verbs.
Incorrect. に marks destination, time, or location of existence.
Incorrect. へ marks direction of movement.

title: 質問の「か」 (Question Sentence Marker 〜ですか)
meaning: Make a polite question with sentence-final か.
connection: Nですか; question word + ですか
nuance: Add か to a polite statement without English-style inversion. For an information question, keep the unknown item in its usual position: 専攻は何ですか asks what the major is. Answer with the requested information; はい/いいえ alone fits a yes/no question, not what/when. Known topics may be omitted. 何 is なん immediately before です; other contexts have なに or fixed readings. Japanese polite questions commonly end in 。 rather than requiring ?.
keyTakeaway: Statement + か asks a question; a question word asks for specific information.

sentences.japanese: 専攻は何ですか。「日本語です。」
sentences.english: What is your major? 'It is Japanese.'
sentences.literal: Major topic what is question? Japanese is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Interrogative 何 directly takes ですか.

quiz.question: 今何時（　　）。「午後二時です。」
quiz.translation: What time is it now? 'It is 2:00 PM.'
quiz.grammarFocus: Question particle か
quiz.ruleHint: Nですか; question word + ですか

explanations.reason: Correct! ですか forms a standard polite question asking the time.
でした is a past statement ending, not the present question ですか.
Incorrect. でして is te-form of copula.
Incorrect. ですね seeks confirmation ('isn't it?'), not an open inquiry.

title: Noun1 の Noun2 (Noun Modification, Possession & Affiliation)
meaning: Particle の connects two nouns where Noun1 modifies, describes, or possesses Noun2 ('Noun1's Noun2' or 'Noun2 of Noun1').
connection: Noun1 (Modifier/Owner) + の + Noun2 (Main item)
nuance: MODIFIER FIRST: Japanese strictly places the modifier before の: 日本の大学 (Japanese university), 私の友達 (my friend).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Owner/Category] の [Item]. The main noun is ALWAYS at the end!

sentences.japanese: たけしさんはさくら大学の学生です。
sentences.english: Takeshi-san is a student of Sakura University.
sentences.literal: Takeshi topic Sakura-University's student is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Affiliation: Sakura University modifies student.

quiz.question: これは私の母（　　）写真です。
quiz.translation: This is a photo of my mother.
quiz.grammarFocus: Possessive / Attribute particle の
quiz.ruleHint: Noun1 (Modifier/Owner) + の + Noun2 (Main item)

explanations.reason: Correct! の connects the subject of the photo (母) to the photo itself (写真).
Incorrect. に marks indirect objects, destinations, or specific time.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects of action verbs.
Incorrect. と means 'and' or 'with'.

title: 時間と年齢 (Telling Time with 〜時・〜分 and Age with 〜歳)
meaning: Formulas for hours (〜時 / じ), minutes (〜分 / ふん・ぷん), and age (〜歳 / さい) including critical phonological irregularities.
connection: Number + 時 (Hour) | Number + 分 (Minutes) | Number + 歳 (Age)
nuance: Hours: 四時よじ、七時しちじ、九時くじ. Minutes include 一分いっぷん、三分さんぷん、四分よんぷん、六分ろっぷん、八分はっぷん、十分じゅっぷん／じっぷん. Ages include 一歳いっさい、八歳はっさい、十歳じゅっさい／じっさい and 二十歳はたち. 何時なんじ asks the time; 何歳なんさい or おいくつ asks age. 半 after the hour means half past. Learn the actual counter reading rather than deriving it mechanically from the independent number.
keyTakeaway: Learn standard time readings: 四時よじ、七時しちじ、九時くじ. 七時 can also be read ななじ to avoid ambiguity in some contexts. 二十歳 is はたち; counter sound changes need separate practice.

sentences.japanese: 今、午前九時半です。私は十九歳です。
sentences.english: Right now, it is 9:30 AM. I am nineteen years old.
sentences.literal: Now AM 9-hour-half is. I 19-years-old am.
sentences.nuanceNote: 九時 is read くじ; 半 means half past.

quiz.question: 会議は午後（　　）から始まります。
quiz.translation: The meeting starts from 4:00 PM.
quiz.grammarFocus: Irregular hour reading 四時 (よじ)
quiz.ruleHint: Number + 時 (Hour) | Number + 分 (Minutes) | Number + 歳 (Age)

explanations.reason: Correct! 4 o'clock is strictly read as よじ (yoji).
Incorrect. よんじ is a common learner error but does not exist in standard Japanese.
四時 has the conventional reading よじ. The general number reading し does not carry over to this counter combination; do not invent an etymological reason.
Incorrect. ななじ is 7, not 4.

title: これ・それ・あれ・どれ (Thing Demonstrative Pronouns)
meaning: Standalone pronouns indicating physical things relative to speaker and listener: これ (near speaker), それ (near listener), あれ (far from both), どれ (which one).
connection: これ / それ / あれ / どれ + は / が / を (Standalone Pronouns)
nuance: STANDALONE RULE: これ/それ/あれ/どれ stand alone as independent nouns. They CANNOT directly modify a noun (you cannot say 'これ本' ❌; that requires 'この本').
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: これ/それ/あれ/どれ stand ALONE. こ (me), そ (you), あ (far away), ど (which?).

sentences.japanese: これは日本のペンです。あれはアメリカのペンです。
sentences.english: This is a Japanese pen. That one over there is an American pen.
sentences.literal: This topic Japan's pen is. That-over-there America's pen is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Spatial contrast between proximal and distal items.

quiz.question: 指さした物について質問します。「（　　）は誰の傘ですか。」
quiz.translation: Pointing at an object: Whose umbrella is this?
quiz.grammarFocus: Demonstrative pronoun それ
quiz.ruleHint: これ / それ / あれ / どれ + は / が / を (Standalone Pronouns)

explanations.reason: これ stands alone and refers to the indicated object.
この requires a following noun; このは is not this construction.
ここで marks an action location and cannot identify an umbrella here.
ここに marks a location of existence, not the indicated object.

title: この・その・あの・どの + Noun (Pre-Noun Demonstrative Modifiers)
meaning: Demonstrative determiners that must immediately precede and specify a noun: この (this N), その (that N near you), あの (that N over there), どの (which N).
connection: この / その / あの / どの + Noun
nuance: MUST HAVE A NOUN: Unlike これ which is an independent noun, この CANNOT stand by itself. Saying 'このは私の' ❌ is ungrammatical; must be 'この時計は私の'.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: この・その・あの・どの MUST be glued to a following Noun!

sentences.japanese: あの時計はいくらですか。「三千円です。」
sentences.english: How much is that watch over there? 'It is 3,000 yen.'
sentences.literal: That watch-over-there how-much is? 3000-yen is.
sentences.nuanceNote: あの directly modifies noun 時計.

quiz.question: 「その辞書」の意味になる形を選んでください。すみません、（　　）辞書を見せてください。
quiz.translation: Choose the form meaning that dictionary: Please show me that dictionary.
quiz.grammarFocus: Pre-noun determiner その
quiz.ruleHint: この / その / あの / どの + Noun

explanations.reason: その directly modifies 辞書.
それ is a standalone pronoun.
そこ means a place and does not directly modify 辞書.
その already modifies a noun; do not add の.

title: ここ・そこ・あそこ・どこ (Place Demonstrative Pronouns)
meaning: Demonstrative locational nouns indicating places: ここ (here), そこ (there near you), あそこ (over there), どこ (where).
connection: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ + は / に / で
nuance: PHONETIC IRREGULARITY: Notice the pattern: こ, そ, but あそこ (NOT あこ ❌)! Interrogative is どこ.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Note the irregularity: ここ, そこ, あそこ (with -そ- in the middle!), どこ.

sentences.japanese: 図書館はどこですか。「あそこです。」
sentences.english: Where is the library? 'It is over there.'
sentences.literal: Library topic where is? Over-there is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Inquiring place with どこ; answering with distant place あそこ.

quiz.question: お手洗いは（　　）ですか。「あちらのエレベーターの隣です。」
quiz.translation: Where is the restroom? 'It is next to the elevator over there.'
quiz.grammarFocus: Locational interrogative どこ
quiz.ruleHint: ここ / そこ / あそこ / どこ + は / に / で

explanations.reason: Correct! どこ is the place interrogative meaning 'where'.
Incorrect. どれ means 'which item among 3+'.
Incorrect. だれ means 'who'.
Incorrect. どう means 'how'.

title: 助詞「も」 (Inclusive Particle 'Also / Too')
meaning: Indicates inclusion: equates the predicate for a new topic to that of a previously mentioned entity ('X is also Y').
connection: Noun + も (Directly replaces は, が, or を!)
nuance: In basic also constructions, も usually replaces は, が or を; it follows particles such as に and で. Literary/emphatic をも exists, so do not treat the beginner replacement rule as a ban in every register.
keyTakeaway: In basic also constructions, も usually replaces は, が or を; it follows particles such as に and で. Literary/emphatic をも exists, so do not treat the beginner replacement rule as a ban in every register.

sentences.japanese: メアリーさんはアメリカ人です。ロバートさんもアメリカ人です。
sentences.english: Mary is an American. Robert is also an American.
sentences.literal: Mary topic American is. Robert also American is.
sentences.nuanceNote: も replaces は to establish shared national identity.

quiz.question: 私（　　）学生です。田中さんと同じです。
quiz.translation: I am a student too, like Tanaka.
quiz.grammarFocus: Particle も replacing direct object
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + も (Directly replaces は, が, or を!)

explanations.reason: も adds me to the group: also a student.
を is an object marker, not the topic/addition here.
に does not form this copula sentence.
で cannot form this copula sentence here.

title: じゃないです / じゃありません (Negative Copula: Is Not)
meaning: Polite non-past negative form of copula です: 'is not / am not / are not'.
connection: Noun / な-adj + じゃないです (Conversational) / じゃありません (Formal)
nuance: REGISTER DIFFERENCE: じゃないです is standard polite spoken Japanese. じゃありません is slightly more formal. ではありません is conservative written/speech style.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Negative of です is じゃないです (or じゃありません). Connects to nouns and な-adjectives.

sentences.japanese: 山田さんは留学生じゃありません。先生です。
sentences.english: Yamada-san is not an international student. He is a teacher.
sentences.literal: Yamada topic international-student is-not. Teacher is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite denial of category followed by affirmative correction.

quiz.question: 私は一年生（　　）。三年生です。
quiz.translation: I am not a first-year student. I am a third-year student.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative copula じゃありません
quiz.ruleHint: Noun / な-adj + じゃないです (Conversational) / じゃありません (Formal)

explanations.reason: Correct! じゃありません (or じゃないです) is the polite negative copula for nouns.
Incorrect. ありません is for inanimate existence (there isn't), not noun identity.
Incorrect. ないでした is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. でした is past affirmative ('was').

title: 〜ます / 〜ません (Polite Non-Past Affirmative & Negative)
meaning: The standard polite verbal ending for present habitual actions and future actions: 〜ます (affirmative) and 〜ません (negative).
connection: Verb stem (ます-stem) + ます / ません
nuance: NON-PAST INCLUDES FUTURE: Japanese has only two grammatical tenses: past and non-past. 食べます means 'I eat (habitually)' OR 'I will eat (future)'.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + ます = Present habit OR future plan. Negative = 〜ません.

sentences.japanese: 私は毎朝コーヒーを飲みますが、お茶は飲みません。
sentences.english: I drink coffee every morning, but I do not drink tea.
sentences.literal: I every-morning coffee drink but, tea drink-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Habitual affirmative and negative actions.

quiz.question: 今日は休みなので、会社には行き（　　）。
quiz.translation: It is a day off, so I will not go to the office.
quiz.grammarFocus: Polite non-past negative 〜ません
quiz.ruleHint: Verb stem (ます-stem) + ます / ません

explanations.reason: The polite negative of 行きます is 行きません.
Plain negative is 行かない, not 行きない.
行きなく is not a valid conjugation.
行きまない is not a valid conjugation.

title: 〜ませんか (Polite Invitation: Won't You? / Would You Like To?)
meaning: Invites the listener to do an activity together politely: 'Won't you...? / Would you like to...?'
connection: V-stem (ます-stem) + ませんか
nuance: ませんか is a standard polite invitation; it does not inherently imply a date. It can also be a literal negative question, so use context. ましょう suggests proceeding together or accepts an invitation. When declining politely, Japanese often gives a reason or trails off with ちょっと rather than using a blunt refusal.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + ませんか = The golden Japanese polite invitation! (一緒に食べませんか = Won't you eat with me?).

sentences.japanese: 今度の週末、一緒に美術館へ行きませんか。「ええ、ぜひ！」
sentences.english: Won't you go to the art museum together this coming weekend? 'Yes, by all means!'
sentences.literal: This-time's weekend, together art-museum go-won't-you? Yes, definitely!
sentences.nuanceNote: Warm invitation paired with enthusiastic agreement.

quiz.question: 少し疲れましたね。喫茶店でお茶を（　　）ませんか。
quiz.translation: We've gotten a bit tired, haven't we? Won't you drink some tea at a cafe?
quiz.grammarFocus: Polite invitation 〜ませんか with verb stem
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます-stem) + ませんか

explanations.reason: Correct! 飲む stem is 飲み, connecting to ませんか (飲みませんか).
Incorrect. 飲む is dictionary form; cannot connect to ませんか.
Incorrect. 飲んで is te-form.
Incorrect. 飲ま is negative stem.

title: 〜ました・〜ませんでした・〜でした (Polite Past Tense of Verbs & Copula)
meaning: Past tense for verbs (〜ました / 〜ませんでした) and noun/adjectival predicates (〜でした / 〜じゃありませんでした).
connection: Verb stem + ました / ませんでした | Noun / な-adj + でした / じゃありませんでした
nuance: Standard polite past negative forms include じゃありませんでした and じゃなかったです. Do not use じゃないでした as the standard conjugation.
keyTakeaway: Standard polite past negative forms include じゃありませんでした and じゃなかったです. Do not use じゃないでした as the standard conjugation.

sentences.japanese: 昨日は雨でした。私はどこへも行きませんでした。
sentences.english: Yesterday was rainy. I did not go anywhere.
sentences.literal: Yesterday rain was. I anywhere go-past-neg.
sentences.nuanceNote: Past state of weather and past negation of activity.

quiz.question: 昨夜は十二時まで日本語を（　　）。とても眠かったです。
quiz.translation: Last night I studied Japanese until 12 o'clock. I was very sleepy.
quiz.grammarFocus: Verb past tense 〜ました
quiz.ruleHint: Verb stem + ました / ませんでした | Noun / な-adj + でした / じゃありませんでした

explanations.reason: Correct! 勉強する past form is 勉強しました.
Incorrect. 勉強します is present/future non-past.
Incorrect. 勉強でした uses copula past without verb inflection.
Incorrect. 勉強しでした is ungrammatical hybrid.

title: 位置の名詞 (Spatial Postpositions: 上・下・前・後ろ・中・隣・近く・間)
meaning: Spatial relational nouns indicating position relative to a reference point: X の [上/下/前/後ろ/中/隣/間] に.
connection: Reference Noun + の + [上 / 下 / 前 / 後ろ / 中 / 隣 / 近く / 間] + に
nuance: 隣 identifies an adjacent neighbor; 近く means nearby. 間 places something between reference points. Do not infer an object's position from a sentence that provides no spatial context.
keyTakeaway: 隣 identifies an adjacent neighbor; 近く means nearby. 間 places something between reference points. Do not infer an object's position from a sentence that provides no spatial context.

sentences.japanese: 猫が机の下で寝ています。銀行は郵便局と本屋の間にあります。
sentences.english: A cat is sleeping under the desk. The bank is between the post office and bookstore.
sentences.literal: Cat desk-under sleeping-is. Bank post-office and bookstore's between exists.
sentences.nuanceNote: Relational location followed by action/existence verbs.

quiz.question: 鍵はかばん（　　）中にあります。
quiz.translation: The key is inside the bag.
quiz.grammarFocus: Spatial noun 中 (inside)
quiz.ruleHint: Reference Noun + の + [上 / 下 / 前 / 後ろ / 中 / 隣 / 近く / 間] + に

explanations.reason: A reference noun connects to 中 with の.
を does not modify 中.
が does not modify 中 here.
と does not express inside the bag.

title: 好き（な） / 嫌い（な） (Expressing Likes and Dislikes with が)
meaning: Like or dislike something. In the basic construction, the liked item takes が; contrast can use は.
connection: [Person] は [Item] が 好きです / 嫌いです (Adjectival predicates)
nuance: 好き and 嫌い are な-adjectives, unlike the English verbs like and dislike. The basic pattern is 私はNが好きです. For a contrast, Nは好きです is also possible. Before a noun use な: 好きな本. For an action, nominalize its clause: 本を読むのが好きです. Avoid treating が as a rule for every construction containing 好き.
keyTakeaway: Basic pattern: Nが好き／嫌いです. When nominalizing an action, keep its object: 本を読むのが好きです.

sentences.japanese: 私は辛い食べ物が大好きですが、甘いお菓子はあまり好きじゃありません。
sentences.english: I love spicy food, but I don't like sweet snacks very much.
sentences.literal: I spicy food like-very but, sweet snacks not-very like-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Target of affection marked with が.

quiz.question: ロバートさんは日本の歴史（　　）とても好きです。
quiz.translation: Robert-san likes Japanese history very much.
quiz.grammarFocus: Object marker が with 好き
quiz.ruleHint: [Person] は [Item] が 好きです / 嫌いです (Adjectival predicates)

explanations.reason: Correct! Target of 好き requires particle が.
Incorrect. を is an English calque trap; 好き is an adjective, not a transitive verb.
Incorrect. に indicates direction/time.
Incorrect. で indicates location/means.

title: 〜ましょう / 〜ましょうか (Volitional Suggestion: Let's / Shall We?)
meaning: Proposes action enthusiastically: 〜ましょう ('Let's do it!') or offers assistance/mutual decision: 〜ましょうか ('Shall we do it? / Shall I help?').
connection: V-stem (ます-stem) + ましょう / ましょうか
nuance: TWO USES OF 〜ましょうか: 1) Suggesting mutual action ('Shall we take a break?'). 2) Offering personal assistance ('Shall I carry your bag?').
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + ましょう = Let's do it! V-stem + ましょうか = Shall we? / Shall I help?

sentences.japanese: 荷物が重そうですね。手伝いましょうか。「ありがとうございます！」
sentences.english: Your luggage looks heavy. Shall I help you? 'Thank you so much!'
sentences.literal: Luggage heavy-looks. Shall-I-help? Thank-you!
sentences.nuanceNote: Offering courteous assistance to someone in need.

quiz.question: 雨が止みましたね。公園を少し（　　）ましょう。
quiz.translation: The rain has stopped, hasn't it? Let's take a walk in the park for a bit.
quiz.grammarFocus: Suggestion 〜ましょう with verb stem
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます-stem) + ましょう / ましょうか

explanations.reason: Correct! 散歩する stem is 散歩し + ましょう (散歩しましょう = Let's take a walk).
Incorrect. 散歩する is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 散歩して is te-form.
Incorrect. 散歩した is past form.

title: 〜てください (Polite Request: Please Do)
meaning: Politely instructs or requests the listener to perform an action for instruction, guidance, or courtesy: 'Please do X'.
chapter: Lesson 6: A Day in Robert's Life
connection: V-て + ください
nuance: REGISTER WARNING: Because ください carries an underlying mild command tone ('do this for me'), saying it to high superiors (professors, boss, clients) can sound overly direct. Use 〜ていただけませんか instead.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + ください = Please do X. Connects strictly to te-form!

sentences.japanese: 教科書の三十五ページを開けてください。
sentences.english: Please open your textbook to page 35.
sentences.literal: Textbook's 35-page open please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Standard classroom instructional request.

quiz.question: ここにあなたのお名前と電話番号を（　　）ください。
quiz.translation: Please write your name and phone number here.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-て + ください polite request
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + ください

explanations.reason: Correct! 書く connects via te-form 書いて + ください.
Incorrect. 書く is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 書き is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 書いた is past form.

title: 〜てもいいですか (Asking for & Granting Permission: May I?)
meaning: Asking for permission: 'May I do X?' (〜てもいいですか). Granting permission: 'You may do X' (〜てもいいです).
chapter: Lesson 6: A Day in Robert's Life
connection: V-て + もいいですか / もいいです
nuance: LITERAL MEANING: 〜ても (even if I do) + いい (it is good). 'Even if I open the window, is it fine?'
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + もいいですか = May I do this? Granting: V-て + もいいですよ.

sentences.japanese: 部屋が少し暑いですね。窓を開けてもいいですか。「ええ、どうぞ。」
sentences.english: The room is a bit hot, isn't it? May I open the window? 'Yes, please go ahead.'
sentences.literal: Room slightly hot is. Window open-even-if good is question? Yes, please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Courteous permission query before altering shared environment.

quiz.question: このペンを少しの間、（　　）てもいいですか。
quiz.translation: May I borrow this pen for a brief moment?
quiz.grammarFocus: Permission formula 〜てもいいですか
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + もいいですか / もいいです

explanations.reason: Correct! 借りる is a Ru-verb: stem 借り + てもいいですか (借りてもいいですか).
Incorrect. 借る is an archaic form.
The dictionary form does not attach directly to てもいい; use 借りてもいい.
Incorrect. 借りた is past form.

title: 〜から (Stating Reasons / Because - Clause Linker)
meaning: States a subjective explanation or cause: 'Because of X, Y happens' or 'Y happens because of X'.
chapter: Lesson 6: A Day in Robert's Life
connection: Sentence 1 (Reason) + から、 Sentence 2 (Conclusion)
nuance: から follows a reason and introduces its consequence. Nouns and な-adjectives take だから in plain non-past affirmative statements, or ですから politely. Verbs and い-adjectives retain their appropriate plain or polite endings. It can introduce requests and intentions, and it can also give factual reasons; subjective is a tendency in the contrast with ので, not a requirement.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Reason] から、[Result]. Unlike English, the reason comes FIRST!

sentences.japanese: 今日は大事なテストがありますから、早く寝ます。
sentences.english: Because I have an important test today, I will go to bed early.
sentences.literal: Today important test have because, early sleep.
sentences.nuanceNote: Reason precedes the resulting decision.

quiz.question: 明日は朝早く起きます（　　）、今夜はテレビを見ません。
quiz.translation: Because I will wake up early tomorrow morning, I won't watch television tonight.
quiz.grammarFocus: Causal clause linker から
quiz.ruleHint: Sentence 1 (Reason) + から、 Sentence 2 (Conclusion)

explanations.reason: Correct! から links the reason for abstaining from TV.
Incorrect. まで means 'until'.
Incorrect. より indicates comparison.
Incorrect. ほど indicates degree or proportion.

title: 身体の描写 (Describing People's Physical Attributes: 目が大きいです)
meaning: Formula for describing a person's physical features: [Person] は [Body Part] が [Adjective] です ('As for X, their eyes are big').
connection: [Person] は + [Body Part] が + [Adjective] です
nuance: Personは body-partが adjective is a common way to describe someone. A possessive subject such as メアリーさんの髪は長いです is also grammatical; the two sentences frame the topic differently.
keyTakeaway: Personは body-partが adjective is a common way to describe someone. A possessive subject such as メアリーさんの髪は長いです is also grammatical; the two sentences frame the topic differently.

sentences.japanese: 私の妹は目が大きくて、髪が長いです。
sentences.english: My younger sister has big eyes and long hair.
sentences.literal: My younger-sister eyes big-and, hair long-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Natural Japanese body description framing.

quiz.question: 田中さんは背が（　　）です。
quiz.translation: Tanaka is tall.
quiz.grammarFocus: Physical attribute marker が (背が高い)
quiz.ruleHint: [Person] は + [Body Part] が + [Adjective] です

explanations.reason: 高い is the adjective predicate.
高く is a connective/adverbial form.
高さ means height and would change the construction.
高 alone is not the adjective predicate.

title: 形容詞・名詞の「て形」 (Connecting Adjectives & Nouns: 〜くて / 〜で)
meaning: Links multiple qualities or attributes: い-adjectives change final い to くて; な-adjectives and nouns take で.
connection: い-adj (drop い) + くて | な-adj stem + で | Noun + で
nuance: THE II/YOI TE-FORM: いい (good) drops its irregular root and conjugates as よくて (NOT いくて ❌)! な-adjectives take で, exactly like nouns.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: い-adj = 〜くて (いい→よくて). な-adj / Noun = 〜で.

sentences.japanese: この部屋は広くて明るくて、とても静かです。
sentences.english: This room is spacious, bright, and very quiet.
sentences.literal: This room spacious-and bright-and, very quiet-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Chaining two い-adjectives via くて into a terminal な-adjective.

quiz.question: あのカフェはコーヒーが（　　）、値段も安いです。
quiz.translation: That cafe's coffee is delicious, and the price is also cheap.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adjective te-form 〜くて
quiz.ruleHint: い-adj (drop い) + くて | な-adj stem + で | Noun + で

explanations.reason: Correct! おいしい drops い + くて = おいしくて.
Incorrect. おいしいで incorrectly applies noun/na-adj で to an い-adj.
Incorrect. おいしくで is ungrammatical.
おいしいくて incorrectly retains the final い; the correct connective form is おいしくて.

title: V-stem + に行く / に来る (Purpose of Movement: Going to Do)
meaning: Expresses the specific purpose of movement: going (行く), coming (来る), or returning (帰る) in order to perform an action.
connection: V-stem (ます-stem) + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る | Activity Noun + に + 行く
nuance: VERB STEM BEFORE に: Drop ます and append に directly: 食べます → 食べに行く, 買いに行きます. If using an activity noun (買い物, 散歩), attach に directly: 買い物に行く.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Masu-stem] に行く = Going to DO X. Purpose particle is STRICTLY に!

sentences.japanese: デパートへ友達の誕生日プレゼントを買いに行きました。
sentences.english: I went to the department store to buy a birthday present for my friend.
sentences.literal: Department-store friend's birthday present buy-in-order-to went.
sentences.nuanceNote: 買う (stem 買い) + に行きました.

quiz.question: 週末は図書館へ本を（　　）に行きます。
quiz.translation: On weekends I go to the library to return books.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-stem + に行く purpose of movement
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます-stem) + に + 行く / 来る / 帰る | Activity Noun + に + 行く

explanations.reason: Correct! 返す (to return an item) stem is 返し + に行きます.
Incorrect. 返す is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 返して is te-form.
Incorrect. 返した is past form.

title: 〜ないでください (Negative Request: Please Do Not)
meaning: Politely requests or instructs someone to refrain from an action: 'Please do not do X'.
connection: V-ない + でください
nuance: NEGATIVE POLITE REQUEST: Formed from the plain negative ない-form + でください. Very common on signs, exams, and courteous instructions (忘れないでください).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-ない + でください = Please don't do X! (Drop nothing from ない).

sentences.japanese: 図書館の中では大声で話さないでください。
sentences.english: Please do not speak in a loud voice inside the library.
sentences.literal: Library inside loud-voice-in speak-not-please.

tokens.reading: はなさないでください

sentences.nuanceNote: 話す negative 話さない + でください.

quiz.question: まだテスト中ですから、教室から（　　）ないでください。
quiz.translation: Since the test is still ongoing, please do not leave the classroom.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-ない + でください negative request
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない + でください

explanations.reason: Correct! 出る (Ru-verb) negative is 出ない + でください (出ないでください).
Incorrect. 出るない is false conjugation.
Incorrect. 出て is te-form.
Incorrect. 出な is ungrammatical.

title: 動詞の「の」名詞化 (Nominalizing Verbs with の: のが好き / 上手 / 下手)
meaning: Turns an action verb into a noun phrase using の, enabling evaluations of preference or skill: V-plain + のが好き / 上手 / 下手.
connection: V-辞書形 + のが [好き / 嫌い / 上手 / 下手 / 得意 / 苦手] です
nuance: Use の to turn an action clause into a noun-like unit: 本を読むのが好きです. The object particle inside the clause remains を. A dictionary-form clause is usual when describing a general preference or skill. This is not a universal prohibition against が following a verb: conjunction が can follow a predicate to mean but in a different construction.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Verb-Dictionary] + のが + 好き / 上手 / 下手! The particle の acts as 'the act of'.

sentences.japanese: 私はギターを弾くのが大好きですが、歌を歌うのはあまり上手ではありません。
sentences.english: I love playing the guitar, but I am not very good at singing songs.
sentences.literal: I guitar play-nominalizer like-very but, songs sing-nominalizer not-very good is-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Nominalizing musical instruments and singing.

quiz.question: 母は料理を（　　）のがとても上手です。
quiz.translation: My mother is very good at cooking meals.
quiz.grammarFocus: Nominalization V-辞書形 + の
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + のが [好き / 嫌い / 上手 / 下手 / 得意 / 苦手] です

explanations.reason: Correct! V-辞書形 作る connects to nominalizer の (作るのが上手).
Incorrect. 作って is te-form.
Incorrect. 作り is masu-stem.
Incorrect. 作った is past form.

title: もう〜ました vs まだ〜ていません (Already Done vs Have Not Yet Done)
meaning: もう〜ました (Action has already been completed). まだ〜ていません (Action has not yet taken place; still in uncompleted state).
connection: もう + Vました; for not yet completed: まだ + Vていません
nuance: For a not-yet-completed event at the present reference point, use まだVていません. Past negation has other uses in a past narrative; it does not inherently mean the speaker never intended to act.
keyTakeaway: For a not-yet-completed event at the present reference point, use まだVていません. Past negation has other uses in a past narrative; it does not inherently mean the speaker never intended to act.

sentences.japanese: 宿題はもう終わりましたか。「いいえ、まだ終わっていません。」
sentences.english: Have you finished your homework already? 'No, I have not finished it yet.'
sentences.literal: Homework already finished? No, still finished-state-not.

tokens.word: まだ終わっていません
tokens.reading: まだおわっていません

sentences.nuanceNote: Canonical pairing of もう with past vs まだ with progressive negative.

quiz.question: 昼ご飯はもう食べましたか。「いいえ、まだ（　　）。」
quiz.translation: Did you eat lunch already? 'No, I haven't eaten yet.'
quiz.grammarFocus: まだ + V-ていません (Not yet)
quiz.ruleHint: もう + Vました; for not yet completed: まだ + Vていません

explanations.reason: Correct! まだ takes progressive negative 食べていません ('have not eaten yet').
食べませんでした reports a past non-event; it does not express the intended current not-yet-completed state in this answer.
食べません can express a habit or future decision not to eat; here the intended answer is have not eaten yet.
Incorrect. 食べないでした is ungrammatical.

title: 〜つもりだ / つもりです (Stated Personal Intention: Plan To)
meaning: States a conscious, determined personal intention or plan: 'I intend to / I plan to do X'.
connection: V-辞書形 + つもりです (Affirmative plan) | V-ない + つもりです / つもりはありません (Negative plan)
nuance: つもり states an intention and can describe another person's intention when the context supports it. Asking superiors about intentions can sound too direct; person is not a rigid first/second-person-only restriction.
keyTakeaway: つもり states an intention and can describe another person's intention when the context supports it. Asking superiors about intentions can sound too direct; person is not a rigid first/second-person-only restriction.

sentences.japanese: 大学を卒業したら、日本の大学院に進学するつもりです。
sentences.english: Upon graduating from college, I intend to advance to graduate school in Japan.
sentences.literal: College graduate-when, Japan's grad-school advance intend.

tokens.meaning: intend to advance to higher education
tokens.reading: しんがくするつもりです

sentences.nuanceNote: Stating personal academic career intent.

quiz.question: 今年の夏休みは、どこへも旅行に（　　）つもりです。家で勉強します。
quiz.translation: This summer vacation, I intend not to travel anywhere. I will study at home.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative intention V-ない + つもりだ
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + つもりです (Affirmative plan) | V-ない + つもりです / つもりはありません (Negative plan)

explanations.reason: Correct! Negative intention connects via ない-form: 行かないつもりです.
Incorrect. 行く indicates affirmative intent to travel.
Incorrect. 行かないで is te-form.
Incorrect. 行った is past form.

title: 形容詞 + なる (Expressing Change of State: To Become)
meaning: Describes a natural or progressive change of state: 'to become [adjective]' (growing warm, becoming quiet, turning into an adult).
connection: い-adj (drop い) + くなる | な-adj stem + になる | Noun + になる
nuance: ADVERBIAL INFLECTION: い-adjectives change final い to く before なる (暖かくなる). な-adjectives and nouns take に before なる (静かになる, 先生になる).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: い-adj = 〜くなる (暑くなる). な-adj / Noun = 〜になる (元気になる, 医者になる).

sentences.japanese: 春になって、だんだん暖かくなってきましたね。
sentences.english: Spring has arrived, and it has gradually become warm, hasn't it?
sentences.literal: Spring become, gradually warm became-came.

tokens.word: 暖かくなってきました
tokens.reading: あたたかくなってきました

sentences.nuanceNote: Noun + になる and い-adj + くなる.

quiz.question: 薬を飲んだら、痛みがだいぶ（　　）なりました。
quiz.translation: After taking the medicine, the pain became considerably better.
quiz.grammarFocus: Change of state with いい (よくなる)
quiz.ruleHint: い-adj (drop い) + くなる | な-adj stem + になる | Noun + になる

explanations.reason: Correct! いい changes through root よい to become adverbial よく + なりました.
Incorrect. いいに is ungrammatical; い-adjectives take く.
Incorrect. よくに is double adverbial marking.
Incorrect. いいく is invalid root conjugation.

title: 〜たい / 〜たくない (Expressing Desire to Do: Want to Do)
meaning: Want to do an action; たくない means not want to do it.
connection: Vます-stem + たい / たくない / たかった
nuance: Attach たい to the polite stem, then conjugate as an い-adjective: 食べたい、食べたくない、食べたかった. In an ordinary statement this commonly expresses the speaker's own desire, while a question can ask the listener's desire. Third-person desire usually needs evidence/reporting or another appropriate context, such as 食べたがっている or 食べたいと言っている. The object can take を or が in suitable constructions. Wanting something does not itself mean a plan or commitment.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + たい = Want to do! Conjugates as an い-adj. Direct object particle を often becomes が.

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行って、本場のラーメンが食べたいです。
sentences.english: I want to go to Japan and eat authentic ramen.
sentences.literal: Japan-to go, authentic ramen eat-want is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Desire to eat authentic ramen.

quiz.question: 今日はとても疲れたので、何も（　　）たくないです。
quiz.translation: Because I am so tired today, I do not want to do anything.
quiz.grammarFocus: Negative desire 〜たくない with verb stem
quiz.ruleHint: Vます-stem + たい / たくない / たかった

explanations.reason: Correct! する stem is し + たくない (したくない = do not want to do).
Incorrect. する is dictionary form.
Incorrect. して is te-form.
Incorrect. した is past form.

title: 〜ことがある (Past Experiential Aspect: Have Ever Done)
meaning: Have done something before; have had an experience.
connection: V-た + ことがある / あります (Negative: ありません / ない)
nuance: Vたことがある presents a previous occurrence as an experience relevant now; it is not restricted to a life-changing or once-in-a-lifetime event. For a simple report of what you did this morning, use a past sentence instead. The time span can be limited by context. V dictionary + ことがある is a different pattern meaning sometimes do. 一度も + negative emphasizes never.
keyTakeaway: たことがある = have done before; dictionary form + ことがある = sometimes do.

sentences.japanese: 富士山に登ったことがありますか。「ええ、一度あります。」
sentences.english: Have you ever climbed Mt. Fuji? 'Yes, once.'
sentences.literal: Mt-Fuji climbed experience have question? Yes, once have.

tokens.word: 登ったことがありますか
tokens.reading: のぼったことがありますか

sentences.nuanceNote: Lifetime experiential inquiry.

quiz.question: 歌舞伎を（　　）ことがありますか。「いいえ、一度もありません。」
quiz.translation: Have you ever seen Kabuki? 'No, not once.'
quiz.grammarFocus: V-た + ことがある lifetime experience
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + ことがある / あります (Negative: ありません / ない)

explanations.reason: Correct! Experiential aspect requires past form 見た + ことがある.
Incorrect. 見ることがある means 'there are times when I see' (occasional habit), not past experience.
Incorrect. 見て is te-form.
Incorrect. 見 is masu-stem.

title: 〜すぎる (Excessiveness: Too Much / Overdoing)
meaning: Indicates exceeding a proper, healthy, or desirable threshold: 'too [adj]' or 'doing [verb] too much'.
connection: V-stem + すぎる | い-adj (drop い) + すぎる | な-adj stem + すぎる (Conjugates as Ru-verb)
nuance: すぎる means exceeding a suitable degree or amount. It often describes an undesirable excess, but can also be enthusiastic hyperbole, as in おいしすぎる. Attach to the verb stem, the い-adjective stem, or the な-adjective stem. いい becomes よすぎる. The basic negative adjective ない becomes なさすぎる; negative verb combinations need care rather than applying one mechanical rule to every ない.
keyTakeaway: Stem + すぎる; いい→よすぎる. The resulting expression conjugates as a ru-verb.

sentences.japanese: 昨夜はお酒を飲みすぎて、今朝はひどい二日酔いです。
sentences.english: Last night I drank too much alcohol, and this morning I have a terrible hangover.
sentences.literal: Last-night alcohol drink-excessively, this-morning terrible hangover is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Excessive drinking resulting in hangover.

quiz.question: この問題は難し（　　）て、私には全く分かりません。
quiz.translation: This problem is too difficult, so I don't understand it at all.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adjective + すぎる excessiveness
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem + すぎる | い-adj (drop い) + すぎる | な-adj stem + すぎる (Conjugates as Ru-verb)

explanations.reason: Correct! 難しい drops い + すぎて forms 難しすぎて ('too difficult').
Incorrect. そう indicates appearance (難しそう).
Incorrect. やすく indicates ease (難しやすく is nonsense).
Incorrect. がち indicates negative tendency.

title: 〜ので (Reason / Background Circumstance)
meaning: Because; since. Presents a reason or background circumstance.
connection: Plain form + ので | な-adj / Noun + な + ので (Notice the required な!)
nuance: ので often makes a reason sound explanatory and less assertive, including before a polite request. から can also be polite, and ので does not make a claim objectively true. Plain non-past nouns and な-adjectives use な: 雨なので、静かなので. Other endings retain their form: 雨だったので、静かではないので. Polite forms can also occur before ので in polite speech.
keyTakeaway: N/な-adjective non-past affirmative: なので. Choose the register and reason in context.

sentences.japanese: 明日は朝早く出発するので、今夜は準備をして早く寝ます。
sentences.english: Since I will depart early tomorrow morning, I will prepare tonight and go to bed early.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow morning early depart since, tonight prepare early sleep.
sentences.nuanceNote: Objective factual circumstance motivating early rest.

quiz.question: 明日は（　　）なので、一日中家でのんびり過ごします。
quiz.translation: Since tomorrow is a holiday, I will spend the entire day relaxing at home.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + な + ので objective causality
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + ので | な-adj / Noun + な + ので (Notice the required な!)

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun 休み connects via な to ので (休みなので).
Incorrect. 休みの is an invalid connector to ので.
Incorrect. 休みだ cannot attach to ので (must be なので, NOT だので ❌).
Incorrect. 休みに is adverbial.

title: 〜なければいけません / なきゃいけません (Obligation: Must Do / Have to Do)
meaning: Expresses an unavoidable obligation or necessity: 'Must do / Have to do X'. Spoken contraction: 〜なきゃいけません / なきゃ.
connection: V-ない (drop い) + ければいけません / ければなりません
nuance: DOUBLE NEGATIVE LOGIC: Literally 'If I do not do X, it cannot go on'. Spoken casual forms contract heavily: なければ → なきゃ, 食べなきゃ.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Drop final い from ない-form, add ければいけません! Casual: 〜なきゃ.

sentences.japanese: 明日の朝九時までに、レポートを提出しなければいけません。
sentences.english: I must submit the report by 9:00 AM tomorrow morning.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow morning 9-by report submit must.

tokens.word: 提出しなければいけません
tokens.reading: ていしゅつしなければいけません

sentences.nuanceNote: Strict academic obligation.

quiz.question: 熱が高いですから、今日は病院へ（　　）ければいけませんよ。
quiz.translation: Since your fever is high, you must go to the hospital today.
quiz.grammarFocus: Obligation formula 〜なければいけません
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない (drop い) + ければいけません / ければなりません

explanations.reason: Correct! 行く negative stem is 行かな + ければいけません.
Incorrect. 行く is dictionary form.
Incorrect. 行って is te-form.
Incorrect. 行き is masu-stem.

title: 〜でしょう / 〜だろう (Conjecture & Probability: Probably)
meaning: Expresses conjecture or probability without absolute certainty: 'Probably / It will likely be X'. Also used with rising tone to seek agreement ('Right?').
connection: Plain form + でしょう (Polite) / だろう (Plain) [Noun & な-adj attach directly without だ!]
nuance: NO だ BEFORE DESHOU: For nouns and な-adjectives, drop だ completely: 暇でしょう (NOT 暇だでしょう ❌), 雨でしょう (NOT 雨だでしょう ❌).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Attach directly without だ! (雨でしょう = It will probably rain).

sentences.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日は午後から雨が降るでしょう。
sentences.english: According to the weather forecast, it will probably rain from the afternoon tomorrow.
sentences.literal: Weather-forecast according-to, tomorrow afternoon-from rain fall probably.
sentences.nuanceNote: Meteorological conjecture.

quiz.question: 田中さんはよく勉強していますから、明日の試験に（　　）でしょう。
quiz.translation: Tanaka studies hard, so they will probably pass tomorrow's exam.
quiz.grammarFocus: Conjecture 〜でしょう with plain verb
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + でしょう (Polite) / だろう (Plain) [Noun & な-adj attach directly without だ!]

explanations.reason: The dictionary form connects directly to でしょう.
The te-form does not connect directly to でしょう here.
The bare stem does not form the required predicate.
Do not put だ after a finite verb before でしょう.

title: 可能形 (Potential Verbs: Ability & Possibility)
meaning: Expresses that an agent has the ability to do an action or that circumstances permit it.
chapter: Lesson 13: Looking for a Part-time Job
connection: Ru-verbs: 食べる→食べられる | U-verbs: 書く→書ける, 飲む→飲める | Irregular: する→できる, くる→こられる
nuance: The potential expresses ability or possibility. The object often takes が, but を also occurs in suitable constructions; do not treat it as universally wrong. Ru-verbs use られる in the standard form; colloquial ら抜き forms such as 食べれる are common but should be distinguished from the standard forms taught here. Some potential and passive/honorific forms overlap, so context matters.
keyTakeaway: The potential expresses ability or possibility. The object often takes が, but を also occurs in suitable constructions; do not treat it as universally wrong. Ru-verbs use られる in the standard form; colloquial ら抜き forms such as 食べれる are common but should be distinguished from the standard forms taught here. Some potential and passive/honorific forms overlap, so context matters.

sentences.japanese: 漢字が難しくて、新聞がすらすら読めません。
sentences.english: The kanji are difficult, so I cannot read the newspaper smoothly.
sentences.literal: Kanji difficult-being, newspaper smoothly read-cannot.
sentences.nuanceNote: 読む potential negative: 読める → 読めません.

quiz.question: 「食べることができません」という意味です。生魚が食べ（　　）。
quiz.translation: I cannot eat raw fish.
quiz.grammarFocus: 可能形 potential negative
quiz.ruleHint: Ru-verbs: 食べる→食べられる | U-verbs: 書く→書ける, 飲む→飲める | Irregular: する→できる, くる→こられる

explanations.reason: 食べられません is the standard potential negative.
食べさせます is causative: make/let eat.
食べたいです expresses desire.
食べました is past affirmative.

title: 〜し、〜し (Listing Multiple Parallel Reasons)
meaning: Lists two or more complementary reasons leading up to a conclusion or emotion ('Not only... but also...').
chapter: Lesson 13: Looking for a Part-time Job

title: なら (Contextual Limitation Conditional: If It's X / As For X)
meaning: Singles out a specific topic from context: 'If we're talking about X, then... / As for X (though other things might not be)'.

title: ほしい (Expressing Desire for an Object: Want Something)
meaning: Expresses first-person desire to possess a concrete object or commodity: [Item] が ほしい ('I want [Item]').

keyTakeaway: Basic desire for a thing: Nがほしい. Desire to perform an action: V-stem + たい.

sentences.english: For my upcoming birthday, I want a new laptop computer.
sentences.literal: This-time's birthday-on, new laptop want is.

title: 〜かもしれない / 〜かもしんない (Epistemic Possibility: Might / May)
meaning: States that something is possible without guaranteeing it: 'might / may be X' (roughly 50% or less certainty).

nuance: NO だ BEFORE KAMOSHれない: Just like でしょう, nouns and な-adjectives drop だ: 雨かもしれない (NOT 雨だかもしれない ❌), 暇かもしれない.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Attach directly without だ! (風邪かもしれない = Might have caught a cold).

The te-form does not directly connect to かもしれません.

title: 〜たらどうですか (Casual Advice / Suggestion: Why Don't You?)
meaning: Offers a suggestion or recommendation to the listener: 'Why don't you try X? / How about doing X?'.

nuance: たらどうですか offers advice. Depending on tone and context, it may sound critical or presumptuous, especially to someone senior. Choose an appropriately indirect suggestion when needed.

title: 意向形 (The Volitional Form: Casual Let's Do / Self-Resolve)
meaning: The casual plain equivalent of 〜ましょう: 'Let's do X!' In monologue, expresses personal determination: 'I shall do X!'.
connection: Ru-verbs: drop る + よう (食べよう) | U-verbs: change final -u to -ou (行こう, 飲もう) | する→しよう, くる→こよう
nuance: CASUAL COMPANION: In peer conversation, '行こう!' replaces '行きましょう!'. In internal monologue, 'よし、頑張ろう!' expresses resolve.

title: 〜といい (Hoping for Favorable Outcomes: I Hope That...)

For an action under the speaker's control, a potential form can make the desired possibility clearer: 行けるといい. Distinguish wishing from advising with ばいい/たらいい in other contexts.

title: 〜時（とき）の時制 (Tense Nuances in 'When' Clauses: V-る時 vs V-た時)
meaning: Tense distinctions before とき: V-る時 (Action NOT yet completed before main verb) vs V-た時 (Action ALREADY completed before main verb).
connection: V-辞書形 + 時 (Prior/During) | V-た + 時 (After completion)
nuance: With a bounded action, dictionary-form とき commonly locates the main event before completion, while たとき commonly locates it after completion. Compare 日本へ行くとき買った and 日本へ行ったとき買った. This is a relative-time contrast, not a rule that every たとき refers to a finished event: 困ったとき means when in trouble, and 子供だったとき means when I was a child. Interpret tense together with the predicate's meaning and the surrounding situation.
keyTakeaway: Use relative timing and the type of situation; とき is not mechanically before versus after.

title: 〜そうです (Hearsay / Quoting Reports: I Heard That / Reportedly)
meaning: Relays information obtained from external news, reports, or rumors without personal verification: 'I heard that... / Reportedly'.
connection: Plain form + そうです (Noun / な-adj non-past takes だ: 暇だそうです, 雨だそうです)
nuance: CRUCIAL DIFFERENCE FROM CONJECTURE: Appearance: drop い (おいしそう = looks tasty). Hearsay: KEEP い and keep だ (おいしいそうです = I heard it's tasty; 暇だそうです = I heard he's free).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Hearsay attaches to 100% UNCHANGED plain form (including だ for nouns/na-adj)! Drop nothing!

Incorrect. 親切 without だ creates appearance/conjecture ('looks kind').

Incorrect. 親切に is adverbial.

title: 〜たら (Specific & Temporal Conditional: If / When / Once Done)
meaning: Universal conditional: 1) Hypothetical condition ('If X happens, then Y'). 2) Temporal certainty in future ('When / Once X finishes, Y will happen').

keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Formed by adding ら to past た-form! Allows commands and requests in clause B.

title: 自動詞 vs 他動詞 (Intransitive vs Transitive Verb Pairs)
meaning: Pairs of verbs distinguishing self-occurring natural phenomena (自動詞: marked with が) from deliberate actions on an object (他動詞: marked with を).
connection: Entity が 自動詞 (開く, 閉まる, つく, 消える) | Agent が Object を 他動詞 (開ける, 閉める, つける, 消す)
nuance: An intransitive verb describes an event or state without a direct object; a transitive verb takes an object. Intransitive does not prove that an event happened spontaneously, and transitive does not by itself prove deliberate intention.
keyTakeaway: An intransitive verb describes an event or state without a direct object; a transitive verb takes an object. Intransitive does not prove that an event happened spontaneously, and transitive does not by itself prove deliberate intention.

sentences.japanese: 風でドアが閉まりました。寒かったので、私がドアを閉めました。

quiz.ruleHint: Entity が 自動詞 (開く, 閉まる, つく, 消える) | Agent が Object を 他動詞 (開ける, 閉める, つける, 消す)

explanations.reason: Correct! Direct object marker を requires transitive verb つける (stem つけ + ましょう).
Incorrect. つく is intransitive (電気がつく).
Incorrect. 消す means turn off.
Incorrect. 消える is intransitive turn off.

title: 〜と (Natural Consequence & Inevitable Conditional: When / If)
meaning: States an inevitable natural consequence, physical law, or habitual fact: 'Whenever X happens, Y automatically occurs'.

nuance: Conditional と describes a regular consequence or discovery. Requests and intentions are normally not used as its consequence in this sense. Narrative と can also connect actual past actions; not every use is an automatic physical law.
keyTakeaway: Conditional と describes a regular consequence or discovery. Requests and intentions are normally not used as its consequence in this sense. Narrative と can also connect actual past actions; not every use is an automatic physical law.

title: 〜ばよかった (Retrospective Regret: I Should Have Done)
meaning: Expresses retrospective regret or remorse over an unfulfilled action: 'I should have done X (but unfortunately I didn't)'. Negative: 'I shouldn't have done X'.

title: 尊敬語 (Honorific Speech: Special Verbs & Regular Formulas)
meaning: Honorific verbs show respect toward the person whose action is described.
connection: Honorific verb; お + suitable verb stem + になる; some verbs have special forms
nuance: 尊敬語 raises the person performing the action; use it for the person being respected, not to elevate your own ordinary actions. It is not restricted to bosses or older people: customers and other people outside your group can be honored. In business speech to an outsider, your own colleague or manager belongs to your group, so do not automatically honor that manager. Special verbs such as いらっしゃる and おっしゃる have special polite forms: いらっしゃいます and おっしゃいます.
keyTakeaway: Choose the viewpoint and social relation first; honorific language respects the actor.

title: 〜間に vs 〜間 (During a Moment vs Throughout the Entire Duration)

connection: V dictionary/ている, い-adjective, な-adjectiveな, Nの + 間 / 間に
nuance: With 間, the second situation holds or an activity continues through the relevant period. With 間に, an event, completion or change occurs within the period. title: 〜ば (The Hypothetical Conditional: If)
meaning: States a logical or hypothetical condition: 'If X condition is met, then Y occurs'.
connection: Verbs: change final -u to -e + ば (書く→書けば, 食べる→食べれば) | い-adj: drop い + ければ | な-adj / Noun: なら (ば)
nuance: と and ば are not freely interchangeable with たら and なら. In hypothetical action sequences, と normally does not introduce the speaker's request or volition. With ば, compatibility also depends on whether the first predicate is stative/negative and on the subjects. たら is versatile for after-completion requests; なら takes up a premise.

title: 〜のに (Frustrated Concession: Even Though / In Spite Of)

title: 〜ことにする vs 〜ことになる (Personal Decision vs Outside Emergence)

nuance: ことにする emphasizes a decision by an actor. ことになる presents a settled outcome or arrangement without emphasizing who made the decision; it does not prove that the speaker had no choice or that layoffs occurred. ことにしている presents a maintained policy, and ことになっている an established arrangement.

title: 〜うちに (While State Lasts / Before Opportunity Slips)

What becomes unavailable may be the opportunity or the preferred condition, not the physical ability to act at all: cold soup can still be eaten. The final clause commonly expresses an intended action, invitation or request. Nの, な-adjectiveな and い-adjectives have different attachments.

title: 〜うちに (Unnoticed Natural Evolution: While Doing X, Y Emerged)

Contrast the opportunity use, where the final clause tells someone to act before a state changes.

title: 〜ところだ (Temporal Phase: Imminent, In the Midst, or Just Finished)
meaning: Pinpoints the exact temporal boundary: 1) Just about to start (辞書形). 2) In the thick of doing (ている). 3) Just completed moments ago (た形).

nuance: Dictionary form marks just before starting, ている the ongoing stage, and た just after completion. Inside a sentence, the following predicate determines the particle: ところを見られる (be seen in the act), ところで電話が来る (a call at that stage), ところへ客が来る (guests arrive into that situation). Do not confuse temporal Vたところで with the separate concessive pattern meaning even if.

Incorrect. ばかり means only / just.
Incorrect. ほど means extent or proportion.

title: 〜によって / 〜によっては (Depending on / According to Differences)
meaning: Indicates diversity, variety, or contingency: 'Depending on X, things differ / In some cases of X...'.
connection: Noun + によって (異なる, 違う, さまざまだ) | Noun + によっては (Certain specific outcomes)
nuance: によって VS によっては: によって introduces general variety (国によって習慣が違う = Customs differ by country). によっては singles out an extreme or specific contingency (日によっては氷点下になる = On some days it drops below freezing).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Noun + によって = Depending on X, things vary. によっては = In some specific cases of X.

sentences.japanese: 文化や宗教によって、タブーとされる食べ物は大きく異なる。

quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + によっては (Contingent outcome)
quiz.ruleHint: Noun + によって (異なる, 違う, さまざまだ) | Noun + によっては (Certain specific outcomes)

explanations.reason: The supplied は completes によっては.
This duplicates the は already after the blank.
にとって describes an evaluating perspective.
について marks a topic, not variation by constitution.

title: 〜たびに (Every Single Time / Invariable Recurrence)
meaning: Each time X occurs, Y happens.
connection: V dictionary / Nの + たびに
nuance: Highlights a recurring connection between a trigger and a result. The result need not be emotional or surprising. Use this pattern for the recurring relation you wish to assert, rather than treating it as proof that no conceivable exception exists.
keyTakeaway: たびに links repeated occasions with their recurring result.

sentences.japanese: このアルバムを見るたびに、楽しかった学生時代を懐かしく思い出す。

quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary / Nの + たびに

たびを does not link this temporal clause.

title: (〜ば)〜ほど (Proportional Correlation: The More... The More...)
meaning: The more X, the more/less Y; one degree changes with another.
connection: V-ば + V-辞書形 + ほど | い-adj ければ + い-adj + ほど | な-adj なら + な-adj な + ほど | Noun + であればあるほど
nuance: The construction describes a correlation: as one degree increases, another changes. It does not imply a mathematically exact proportional rate. The initial conditional can be omitted: 考えるほど分からなくなる. Repeat the same predicate when using the full pair and preserve the adjective linking form before ほど.

title: 〜かわりに (In Exchange For / Compensation / Instead Of)

title: 〜ためだ / 〜ために (Objective Cause: Due to / Owing to)
meaning: Formal written and broadcast expression stating an objective cause or reason: 'Due to X, consequence Y resulted'.
connection: Plain form + ため（に） (な-adj takes な, Noun takes の: 大雪のために)
nuance: Causal ために is common in factual and formal accounts. It differs from purpose ために. When making a personal request, choose a natural reason/request construction rather than automatically applying a single conjunction rule.

ためを is not this cause linker.

title: 〜ことから (Origin of Name, Judgment, or Fact: Arising from the Fact That)
meaning: Points to the historical origin, observable characteristic, or evidential cue that led to a name, reputation, or deduction: 'Named so / Inferred because of X'.

nuance: NAME ORIGIN & EVIDENTIAL CLUE: Ubiquitous when explaining why places or plants are named: '形が星に似ていることから、星草と呼ばれている' (Called star grass because its shape resembles a star).

nuance: Treats the preceding situation as a relevant premise supporting a judgment, encouragement, request or criticism. The speaker may remind the listener of it; it need not be a fact already explicitly agreed by everyone. んだから is conversational and can sound insistent depending on tone.

title: 〜だらけ (Covered in Mess, Flaws, or Filth: Riddled With / Full Of)
meaning: Covered entirely with an undesirable substance or riddled with flaws: 'covered in mud, full of errors, riddled with debts'.
chapter: 形式整理 J: 意味を広げる形式 (Suffixes & Tendencies)
connection: Noun + だらけ (泥だらけ, 間違いだらけ, ゴミだらけ, 借金だらけ)
nuance: だらけ means full of or covered with many examples of something, commonly unwelcome things such as mistakes or mud. Its negative association is a tendency, not a logical ban on every positive noun.
keyTakeaway: だらけ means full of or covered with many examples of something, commonly unwelcome things such as mistakes or mud. Its negative association is a tendency, not a logical ban on every positive noun.

sentences.japanese: 急いで書いた彼のレポートは、誤字や文法の間違いだらけだった。

title: 〜くらいなら / 〜ぐらいなら (Rather Than Suffer X, I Would Prefer Y)
meaning: If forced to endure an unacceptable condition X, I would far rather do alternative Y (even if Y is also drastic).
connection: V-辞書形 + くらいなら / ぐらいなら
nuance: UNACCEPTABLE ALTERNATIVE: X is considered so awful that the speaker prefers Y. Example: '満員電車に乗るくらいなら、1時間歩くほうがましだ' (Rather than ride a packed train, I'd rather walk an hour).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-る + くらいなら = 'Rather than do X, I'd rather...'. Expresses subjective value choice.

sentences.japanese: 彼に頭を下げて頼むくらいなら、自分で失敗したほうがまだましだ。

sentences.literal: Him-to head lower begging rather-than, by-myself failed better is.

quiz.question: あんな失礼な人に謝る（　　）なら、仕事を辞めたほうがいい。
quiz.translation: Rather than apologize to such a rude person, I'd rather quit my job.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + くらいなら (Preferential aversion)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + くらいなら / ぐらいなら

explanations.reason: Correct! 謝るくらいなら expresses 'Rather than apologize, I'd prefer quitting'.
Incorrect. ほどなら is ungrammatical in this comparative preference structure.
Incorrect. ばかりなら does not express 'rather than'.
Incorrect. だけになら is incorrect.

title: 〜に限る (Nothing Beats / Best Choice)
meaning: Nothing beats X; X is the best choice or best thing to do.
connection: N / V dictionary / Vない + に限る
nuance: This pattern expresses the speaker's subjective recommendation, not an objectively proven ranking. A negative verb recommends avoiding an action: 無理をしないに限る means it is best not to overdo things. やっぱり often accompanies a confident preference. Do not confuse this with Nに限り (restricted to N), Nに限って (specifically/on this occasion, among other uses), or とは限らない (not necessarily). The dictionary verb 限る means to limit; the whole grammar pattern has the best-choice meaning here.
keyTakeaway: に限る = the best choice; に限り = limited to. Read the whole pattern.

sentences.japanese: 風邪を引いたときは、温かいスープを飲んで早く寝るに限る。
sentences.english: When you catch a cold, nothing beats drinking hot soup and getting to sleep early.
sentences.literal: Cold caught when, hot soup drink early sleep is-best.
sentences.nuanceNote: Universal folk wisdom framed as speaker's top recommendation.

quiz.question: 「早く寝るのが一番よい」という意味です。疲れた日は、早く寝るに（　　）。
quiz.translation: On a tiring day, the best thing is to go to bed early.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + に限る (Supreme choice)
quiz.ruleHint: N / V dictionary / Vない + に限る

explanations.reason: に限る gives the subjective best choice.
限って is a connective form and does not complete this sentence.
限りな is not this verb form.
限ら is an unfinished stem.

title: 〜に対して (In Contrast To / While X Is..., Y Is...)
meaning: In contrast to / whereas; also toward a target in a different use.
connection: Noun + に対して | 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + である) + のに対して
nuance: In the contrast use, two subjects or situations are compared; they need not be exact polar opposites. A full predicate uses のに対して. A different use, Nに対して, identifies the target of an action or attitude, such as 客に対して親切だ.
keyTakeaway: In the contrast use, two subjects or situations are compared; they need not be exact polar opposites. A full predicate uses のに対して. A different use, Nに対して, identifies the target of an action or attitude, such as 客に対して親切だ.

title: 〜おかげで vs 〜せいで (Grace of / Due to Fault of)
meaning: Expresses causal attribution: おかげで attributes a positive outcome to a benefactor; せいで blames an adverse outcome on a scapegoat.

nuance: VALUE POLARITY: おかげで = Gratitude ('Thanks to your guidance, I passed!'). せいで = Blame ('Because of the accident, I was late!'). (Ironical usage also exists: お前のせいで/お前のおかげで).

title: 〜さえ〜ば (If Only / Provided That Sole Prerequisite Is Met)

title: たとえ〜ても (Even If / Even Granting That Hypothetical X Occurs)
meaning: Even if X is assumed, Y still holds.
connection: たとえ + Vても / adjectiveくても / Nでも / な-adjectiveでも
nuance: たとえ explicitly introduces a hypothetical concession. The result may be a fact, judgment, intention or recommendation; it need not be the speaker's unshakable resolve. Distinguish a hypothetical case from a known fact, although ても itself can be used with either.
keyTakeaway: The assumed condition does not overturn the conclusion.

quiz.ruleHint: たとえ + Vても / adjectiveくても / Nでも / な-adjectiveでも

explanations.reason: Correct! たとえ pairs with 〜ても to mean 'Even if / Even supposing that'.
Incorrect. まるで pairs with ようだ ('just like').
Incorrect. 決して pairs with negative verbs ('never').
Incorrect. まさか expresses disbelief ('don't tell me...').

title: 〜ように (So That / In Order That - Non-Volitional Objective)
meaning: Expresses an objective or intended state toward which action is directed: 'So that X may become possible / so that X doesn't happen'.
connection: V-辞書形 (Potential / Intransitive non-volitional) / V-ない + ように
nuance: VOLITIONAL CONTRAST: ように takes non-volitional verbs (見える、聞こえる、忘れない, potential verbs). In contrast, ために takes conscious volitional actions by the same subject.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-ない / V-可能形 + ように = 'So that...'. Example: 忘れないようにメモする (Jot down so as not to forget).

title: 〜わけがない (There Is Absolutely No Way That... / Utter Impossibility)
meaning: Expresses the speaker's adamant, logical conclusion that something is completely impossible or out of the question.
connection: 普通形 (な-adj + な/である, Noun + の/である) + わけがない / わけはない
nuance: Expresses the speaker's strong rejection of a possibility, often based on a stated reason. The form does not turn the speaker's belief into an objective or mathematical proof. Contrast わけではない, which denies an inference or a full/general claim without necessarily asserting the opposite.
keyTakeaway: Expresses the speaker's strong rejection of a possibility, often based on a stated reason. The form does not turn the speaker's belief into an objective or mathematical proof. Contrast わけではない, which denies an inference or a full/general claim without necessarily asserting the opposite.

title: 〜わけではない (It Doesn't Mean That... / Partial Negation)
meaning: Softens an assumption or clarifies that while things might appear so, it is not entirely or universally true: 'Not necessarily / It's not that...'.

title: 〜わけにはいかない (Cannot Afford To / Morally or Socially Bound Not To)
meaning: Indicates that even if the speaker wants to do X, social morals, duties, or practical constraints make it utterly impermissible: 'Cannot afford to do / In all conscience I cannot'.

keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-る + わけにはいかない = 'Cannot do (conscience/duty forbids)'. V-ない + わけにはいかない = 'MUST do!'.

title: 〜がる / 〜がっている (Third-Person Manifestation of Desires & Sensations)
meaning: Describes observable behaviors indicating that someone other than the speaker feels an emotion, sensation, or desire.

nuance: がる describes observable indications of a feeling or desire, often about someone else. Reports, quotations and narrative contexts also allow other ways to describe a third person; it is not a blanket ban on third-person adjective predicates.
keyTakeaway: がる describes observable indications of a feeling or desire, often about someone else. Reports, quotations and narrative contexts also allow other ways to describe a third person; it is not a blanket ban on third-person adjective predicates.

meaning: Should; ought to; what one judges appropriate.
connection: V-辞書形 + べきだ / べきではない (する irregular: すべきだ or するべきだ)
nuance: Expresses what is appropriate, expected or advisable from the speaker's viewpoint. It can sound strong or moralizing, but is not restricted to universally agreed moral duties. Both するべき and すべき occur.
keyTakeaway: Expresses what is appropriate, expected or advisable from the speaker's viewpoint. It can sound strong or moralizing, but is not restricted to universally agreed moral duties. Both するべき and すべき occur.

sentences.japanese: 借りたお金は、どんなに親しい友人であっても期日通りに返す（　　）だ。
sentences.english: Money that you have borrowed ought to be repaid right on schedule, no matter how close a friend they may be.
sentences.literal: Borrowed money, how-much close friend even-if schedule-according repay ought-to is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Moral principle governing personal financial integrity.

quiz.question: ミスに気づいたら、すぐに訂正す（　　）です。
quiz.translation: If you notice a mistake, you should correct it promptly.
quiz.grammarFocus: する → すべきだ (Moral imperative)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + べきだ / べきではない (する irregular: すべきだ or するべきだ)

explanations.reason: すべきです expresses what should be done.
べく is a connective form, not the predicate before です here.
べきな is not the predicate form.
べかった is not a conjugation of べき.

title: 〜によると / 〜によれば (According To Source of Information)
meaning: According to a source of information.
connection: Source noun + によると / によれば
nuance: Names the source rather than claiming direct personal observation. It commonly accompanies そうだ, らしい, ということだ and similar reporting endings, but these are not mandatory in every report. Distinguish によって for means, cause, agency or variation.
keyTakeaway: Identify the information source; reported-style endings are common, not obligatory.

sentences.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日の夕方から関東地方全域で大雪になるそうだ。
sentences.english: According to the weather forecast, heavy snow will reportedly blanket the entire Kanto region starting tomorrow evening.
sentences.literal: Weather forecast according-to, tomorrow evening-from Kanto entire heavy-snow become reportedly.

tokens.reading: てんきよほうによると

sentences.nuanceNote: Formal citation of meteorological bulletin.

quiz.question: 今朝の新聞（　　）よると、ガソリン価格が来月から再び値上がりするそうだ。
quiz.translation: According to this morning's newspaper, gasoline prices will reportedly hike again starting next month.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + によると (Citing sources)
quiz.ruleHint: Source noun + によると / によれば

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun + によると is the fixed citation pattern.
Incorrect. でよると does not exist.
Incorrect. をよると is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. へよると is invalid.

title: 〜らしい (Evidential Hearsay vs Typical Archetype)
meaning: Two primary senses: (1) Hearsay/conjecture based on external reports ('apparently'); (2) Exemplifying the quintessence of a quality ('truly typical of / behaving like a real...').
connection: Sense 1 (Conjecture): 普通形 (Noun / な-adj bare) + らしい | Sense 2 (Typicality): Noun + らしい
nuance: らしい has an inference/report sense and a typical-quality sense. In 春らしい, it means characteristic of spring. っぽい describes a perceived resemblance or tendency, often informally; it is not inherently shallow or fake. Determine the sense of らしい from what precedes it and the context.
keyTakeaway: Identify the sense: apparent/report-based inference, or a quality typical of a noun.

sentences.japanese: 桜が咲いてポカポカ暖かくなり、ようやく春らしい季節になった。
sentences.english: With cherry blossoms blooming and pleasantly warm weather, it has finally become a truly spring-like season.
sentences.literal: Cherry-blossoms bloomed pleasantly warm became, at-last spring-like season became.
sentences.nuanceNote: Embodying the ideal aesthetic qualities of springtime.

quiz.question: 負けて悔しいのは分かるが、プロの選手（　　）最後まで堂々と振る舞うべきだ。
quiz.translation: I understand you are frustrated by the loss, but as a professional athlete you ought to carry yourself with dignity until the end.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + らしく (Archetypical conduct)
quiz.ruleHint: Sense 1 (Conjecture): 普通形 (Noun / な-adj bare) + らしい | Sense 2 (Typicality): Noun + らしい

explanations.reason: Correct! 選手らしく means 'in a manner befitting a true athlete'.
Incorrect. 選手そうに is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 選手みたいで implies superficial resemblance rather than true professional conduct.
Incorrect. 選手がちに is meaningless.

title: 〜ことにしている (Habitual Personal Rule / Self-Imposed Policy)
meaning: Indicates a conscious, self-imposed rule or habitual code of conduct that the speaker upholds consistently.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-ない形 + ことにしている
nuance: Presents a maintained personal decision or practice. Compare ようにしている (effort to behave that way) and ことになっている (an established arrangement). The contrast is one of presentation; the latter does not necessarily prove an outside authority made the decision.
keyTakeaway: Presents a maintained personal decision or practice. Compare ようにしている (effort to behave that way) and ことになっている (an established arrangement). The contrast is one of presentation; the latter does not necessarily prove an outside authority made the decision.

sentences.japanese: どんなに忙しくても、毎日必ず30分は読書をすることにしている。
sentences.english: No matter how busy I am, I make it a strict personal rule to read for at least 30 minutes every day.
sentences.literal: How-much busy even-if, every-day definitely 30-minutes reading do-rule-have.

tokens.word: 読書をすることにしている
tokens.meaning: make it a rule to read
tokens.reading: どくしょをすることにしている
tokens.romaji: dokusho o suru koto ni shite iru

sentences.nuanceNote: Disciplined intellectual daily habit.

quiz.question: 環境を守るため、買い物にはマイバッグを持参する（　　）にしている。
quiz.translation: To protect the environment, I make it a policy to bring my own shopping bag when buying goods.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + ことにしている (Personal code)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ない形 + ことにしている

explanations.reason: Correct! 持参することにしている expresses an intentional self-directed eco-friendly habit.
Incorrect. ものにしている does not express personal rules.
Incorrect. わけにしている is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. ところにしている is invalid.

title: 〜つもり (Believing / Acting as If / Contrary to Reality)
meaning: Expresses that the subject acts with the internal belief or mental mindset of X, regardless of whether external reality or others agree.
connection: V-た形 / Noun + の / い-adj / な-adj + な + つもり (Noun modifier)
nuance: CONVICTION VS REALITY: Can convey a subjective illusion: '自分では若いつもりだが、階段で息が切れる' (I feel young in my own mind, but I get out of breath on stairs). Or reproaching someone: '冗談のつもりだった' (I intended it as a joke).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-た / Nounの + つもり = 'In my mind / Believing that I had done so (even if reality differs)'.

sentences.japanese: 鍵を閉めたつもりだったが、帰宅したらドアが開いていてぞっとした。
sentences.english: I was under the firm impression that I had locked the door, but returning home I was terrified to find it wide open.
sentences.literal: Key locked impression-had, home-returned door open-being horrified.
sentences.nuanceNote: Chilling discovery of a mistaken assumption.

quiz.question: 自分では上手に説明した（　　）だったが、誰にも理解してもらえなかった。
quiz.translation: In my own mind I believed I had explained it clearly, but nobody understood me.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-た + つもり (Mistaken subjective impression)
quiz.ruleHint: V-た形 / Noun + の / い-adj / な-adj + な + つもり (Noun modifier)

explanations.reason: Correct! 説明したつもりだった reflects internal conviction contradicted by the listeners' bewilderment.
Incorrect. はずだった means 'was supposed to' (expectation that failed to happen).
Incorrect. わけだった does not express subjective misconception.
Incorrect. ところだった means 'was on the verge of'.

title: お〜になる / ご〜になる (Honorific Respect - Elevating Others' Actions)
meaning: Transforms a regular verb into a respectful honorific (尊敬語) to elevate the actions of an esteemed superior, client, or guest.
chapter: Unit 12: 敬語・待遇表現 (Politeness & Respect)
connection: お + V-stem + になる (wago) | ご + Noun (suru-verb) + になる / なさる (kango)
nuance: Respectful language elevates the person performing an action. Whether a colleague or family member is in-group depends on whom you are addressing; speaking internally about a superior differs from representing your company to an outsider.
keyTakeaway: Respectful language elevates the person performing an action. Whether a colleague or family member is in-group depends on whom you are addressing; speaking internally about a superior differs from representing your company to an outsider.

sentences.japanese: 部長は今朝のニュースをすでにお読みになりましたか。
sentences.english: Department manager, have you already read this morning's news?
sentences.literal: Department-manager morning news already honorably-read became-question?

tokens.word: お読みになりましたか
tokens.reading: およみになりましたか

sentences.nuanceNote: Deferential query directed upward toward department head.

quiz.question: 先生、こちらの新しい資料をもうご（　　）になりましたか。
quiz.translation: Professor, have you already reviewed this new reference material?
quiz.grammarFocus: ご覧になる (Honorific vision)
quiz.ruleHint: お + V-stem + になる (wago) | ご + Noun (suru-verb) + になる / なさる (kango)

explanations.reason: Correct! ご覧になる is the honorific form of 見る ('to look/review').
Incorrect. ご見になる is ungrammatical.
拝見する is humble for an in-group person viewing something; it does not form the teacher-honorifying ご覧になる pattern.
Incorrect. ご見せになる is invalid.

title: お〜する / ご〜する (Humble Deference - Lowering One's Own Actions)
meaning: Transforms an action performed by the speaker into a humble deferential (謙譲語), lowering oneself to demonstrate respect to the recipient.
chapter: Unit 12: 敬語・待遇表現 (Politeness & Respect)
connection: お + V-stem + する / いたす | ご + Noun (suru-verb) + する / いたす
nuance: The お〜する / ご〜する pattern commonly lowers an in-group action directed toward someone respected. The respected person need not be the listener. Not every verb accepts the productive pattern, and some have special forms such as 拝見する. Distinguish humble/polite forms such as 参る, 申す and おる, which can show deference toward the listener without an honored action-recipient.
keyTakeaway: The お〜する / ご〜する pattern commonly lowers an in-group action directed toward someone respected. The respected person need not be the listener. Not every verb accepts the productive pattern, and some have special forms such as 拝見する. Distinguish humble/polite forms such as 参る, 申す and おる, which can show deference toward the listener without an honored action-recipient.

sentences.japanese: 明日の午後に、こちらから改めてお電話いたします。
sentences.english: I will personally telephone you once again tomorrow afternoon.
sentences.literal: Tomorrow afternoon, from-here again humble-phone will-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite corporate commitment to follow up by phone.

quiz.question: 私が先生に資料をお送り（　　）。
quiz.translation: I will send the materials to my teacher.
quiz.grammarFocus: ご + Kango + ください (Polite client request)
quiz.ruleHint: お + V-stem + する / いたす | ご + Noun (suru-verb) + する / いたす

explanations.reason: お送りする is the humble construction.
お送りになる is respectful and inappropriate for the speaker's own action here.
お送りされる is not the intended humble construction.
お送りなります is not a valid form.

title: 〜ところだった (Was on the Very Verge Of / Narrowly Escaped)
meaning: Indicates that an undesirable disaster or drastic event almost occurred, but was averted in the nick of time: 'I almost / was on the verge of...'.
chapter: 形式整理 C: ところの形式 (Form C: Tokoro)
connection: V-辞書形 + ところだった (often paired with もう少しで, 危うく)
nuance: NARROW ESCAPE: Almost always paired with adverbs like もう少しで (by a hair's breadth) or 危うく (narrowly): 'もう少しで終電に乗り遅れるところだった' (I almost missed the last train).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: もう少しで + V-る + ところだった = 'Narrow escape! Almost happened but thank goodness it didn't!'.

sentences.japanese: 足元が滑って、危うく階段から転がり落ちるところだった。
sentences.english: My footing slipped, and I came within a hair's breadth of tumbling down the stairs.
sentences.literal: Footing slipped, narrowly stairs-from tumble-down verge-was.

tokens.word: 転がり落ちるところだった
tokens.meaning: was on the verge of tumbling down
tokens.reading: ころがりおちるところだった

sentences.nuanceNote: Heart-stopping near-miss on a steep staircase.

quiz.question: 友達が声をかけてくれなかったら、大事な約束を（　　）ところだった。
quiz.translation: If my friend hadn't called out to remind me, I would have completely forgotten my important appointment.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-る + ところだった (Averted outcome)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + ところだった (often paired with もう少しで, 危うく)

explanations.reason: Correct! 辞書形 忘れる + ところだった expresses an action that was narrowly averted.
忘れたところだった would mean had just forgotten; it does not express the averted event required by this context.
Incorrect. 忘れてところだった is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. 忘れないところだった conveys the opposite meaning.

title: 〜気味 (Slight Negative Tinge / Feeling Somewhat...)
meaning: Indicates a subtle, mild onset of an undesirable physical, mental, or situational condition: 'a touch of / feeling slightly...'.
chapter: 形式整理 J: 意味を広げる形式 (Suffixes & Tendencies)
connection: V-stem + 気味 (ぎみ) | Noun + 気味 (風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 太り気味, 遅れ気味)
nuance: 気味 describes a slight tendency or degree of a condition, often unwelcome: 風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 緊張気味. It need not mean the beginning of an illness; it can describe an ongoing mild condition. Attachment is conventional rather than freely possible with every noun or stem.
keyTakeaway: 気味 describes a slight tendency or degree of a condition, often unwelcome: 風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 緊張気味. It need not mean the beginning of an illness; it can describe an ongoing mild condition. Attachment is conventional rather than freely possible with every noun or stem.

sentences.japanese: 最近残業続きで疲れ気味なので、今週末は家でゆっくり休みたい。
sentences.english: Because I've been feeling somewhat worn out from consecutive overtime lately, I want to rest peacefully at home this weekend.
sentences.literal: Recently overtime-continuation-due-to fatigue-touch-being, this-weekend home peacefully want-to-rest.
sentences.nuanceNote: Mild exhaustion prompting weekend recuperation.

quiz.question: 朝から喉が痛くて少し（　　）気味なので、早めに薬を飲んで寝ます。
quiz.translation: My throat has been hurting since morning and I have a touch of a cold, so I will take medicine early and go to sleep.
quiz.grammarFocus: Noun + 気味 (Nascent symptom)
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem + 気味 (ぎみ) | Noun + 気味 (風邪気味, 疲れ気味, 太り気味, 遅れ気味)

explanations.reason: Correct! 風邪気味 (かぜぎみ) is the classic idiom for having a mild touch of a cold.
Incorrect. 病気気味 is not standard Japanese.
Incorrect. 熱気味 is unnatural (one says 微熱がある).
Incorrect. 痛い気味 is ungrammatical (adjectives do not attach directly to 気味).

title: 〜がち (Prone To / Habitual Unfortunate Tendency)
meaning: Indicates a recurring, unwanted tendency to happen frequently or slip into an undesirable state: 'tending to / prone to / easily falling into...'.
chapter: 形式整理 J: 意味を広げる形式 (Suffixes & Tendencies)
connection: V-stem + がち | Noun + がち (留守がち, 曇りがち, 遠慮がち, 忘れがち)
nuance: がち describes a recurring tendency, often unwelcome. It attaches to selected nouns and verb stems and forms combinations such as 病気がちだ and 忘れがちなこと. 気味 describes a slight degree/state and is not restricted to physical symptoms. The two can overlap in some contexts; do not treat every similar-looking alternative as ungrammatical.
keyTakeaway: がち describes a recurring tendency, often unwelcome. It attaches to selected nouns and verb stems and forms combinations such as 病気がちだ and 忘れがちなこと. 気味 describes a slight degree/state and is not restricted to physical symptoms. The two can overlap in some contexts; do not treat every similar-looking alternative as ungrammatical.

sentences.japanese: スマートフォンに夢中になると、ついつい夜更かしをしがちだ。
sentences.english: When absorbed in one's smartphone, one is terribly prone to inadvertently staying up late.
sentences.literal: Smartphone absorbed become, inadvertently staying-up-late prone-to-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: Common behavioral vulnerability in modern life.

quiz.question: 最近、仕事が忙しくて、約束を忘れ（　　）です。
quiz.translation: Recently I have been busy with work and tend to forget appointments.
quiz.grammarFocus: V-stem + がち (Frequent behavioral tendency)
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem + がち | Noun + がち (留守がち, 曇りがち, 遠慮がち, 忘れがち)

explanations.reason: V-stem + がちです describes a tendency.
がちな modifies a following noun.
がちに is adverbial, not the predicate before です.
がちの does not form this predicate.

title: 〜に際して / 〜にあたって (Upon the Occasion Of / At the Inception Of)
meaning: Formal expression used when initiating an important event, official occasion, or milestone: "On the occasion of / Prior to commencing X".
connection: V-辞書形 + に際して / にあたって | Noun + に際して / にあたって
