quiz.grammarFocus: V-stem + まい (Steadfast negative determination)
quiz.ruleHint: V dictionary + まい; ru-verbs also stem + まい; するまい / すまい / しまい; 来るまい / 来まい

explanations.reason: するまい expresses negative resolve.
するず is not a negative form.
するぬで is not the required construction.
するなく is not a negative form.

title: X は Y です (X is Y / Topic & Copula)
meaning: Identify or describe a topic: as for X, it is Y.
connection: X は noun です; noun です is enough when the topic is understood.
nuance: は is written は but pronounced わ when it marks the topic. It tells the listener what the statement is about; it is not simply a replacement for the English subject. If both speakers already know the topic, omit it: 学生です can mean I am a student, she is a student, or they are students, depending on context. Japanese nouns generally do not require a/an and do not automatically change for plural number. です makes the noun predicate polite and non-past; it does not change with person or number. Do not append です to an ordinary finite verb such as 行くです. Adjectives have their own patterns, introduced later: 静かです and 高いです, but not 静かだです or 高いだです. Use a name/title rather than repeatedly translating English you as あなた.
keyTakeaway: State the topic only when needed; put the identifying noun before polite です.

sentences.japanese: 私はカリフォルニア大学の留学生です。
sentences.english: I am an international student at the University of California.
sentences.literal: I topic UC's international-student am.
sentences.nuanceNote: Standard polite self-introduction formula.

quiz.question: 田中さん（　　）日本人です。
quiz.translation: Tanaka-san is Japanese.
quiz.grammarFocus: Topic marker は
quiz.ruleHint: X は noun です; noun です is enough when the topic is understood.

explanations.reason: Correct! は marks Tanaka-san as the topic being identified as Japanese.
Incorrect. を marks direct objects of action verbs, not copula topics.
Incorrect. に indicates direction, time, or location of existence.
Incorrect. へ indicates direction of movement.

title: 動詞の３分類 (The Three Verb Groups: Ru, U, & Irregular)
meaning: Japanese verbs are strictly classified into Ru-verbs (一段), U-verbs (五段), and Irregular verbs (する, くる).
connection: Ru-verbs: stem + ます | U-verbs: u-vowel changes to i-vowel + ます | Irregular: する→します, くる→きます
nuance: Not every verb ending in る is a Ru-verb! Verbs like 帰る (かえる - to return) and 知る (しる - to know) end in る but are 五段 U-verbs (帰ります, 知ります).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Ru-verbs drop る. U-verbs change final u to i (行く→行きます, 飲む→飲みます).

sentences.japanese: 毎晩図書館で日本語を勉強します。
sentences.english: I study Japanese in the library every night.
sentences.literal: Every-night library-at Japanese study-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: 勉強する is an irregular compound verb (勉強します).

quiz.question: 明日友達と映画を（　　）ます。
quiz.translation: I will watch a movie with a friend tomorrow.
quiz.grammarFocus: Ru-verb stem connection to ます
quiz.ruleHint: Ru-verbs: stem + ます | U-verbs: u-vowel changes to i-vowel + ます | Irregular: する→します, くる→きます

explanations.reason: Correct! 見る drops る to form 見ます.
Incorrect. Cannot retain dictionary る before ます.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot attach directly to ます.
Incorrect. 見ら is part of passive/potential, not polite stem.

title: て形 (The Te-Form & Polite Requests 〜てください)
meaning: The fundamental connective form of Japanese verbs, used for requests (〜てください), permission (〜てもいい), prohibition (〜てはいけない), and sequence.
chapter: Lesson 6: A Day in Robert's Life
connection: う・つ・る→って | む・ぶ・ぬ→んで | く→いて (行く→行って!) | ぐ→いで | す→して | る(一段)→て
nuance: CRITICAL EXCEPTION: 行く (iku) does NOT become いいて. It irregularly contracts to 行って (itte)!
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + ください = Please do. Prohibited: V-て + はいけません = Must not.

table.title: The Te-Form (て形) Conjugation Matrix
table.subtitle: The foundational gateway for ~ている, ~てから, ~てもいい, ~てはいけない, and ~てしまう.

rows.label: Group 1: う・つ・る
cells: 買う (kau), 待つ (matsu), 取る (toru)
買って, 待って, 取って
買った, 待った, 取った
う・つ・る → って / った (Small つ + て)
rows.note: Classic rhythm: "u, tsu, ru becomes tte"

rows.label: Group 1: む・ぶ・ぬ
cells: 飲む (nomu), 遊ぶ (asobu), 死ぬ (shinu)
飲んで, 遊んで, 死んで
飲んだ, 遊んだ, 死んだ
む・ぶ・ぬ → んで / んだ (Voiced ん + で)
rows.note: Voiced consonants always take で, not て.

rows.label: Group 1: く / ぐ
cells: 書く (kaku), 泳ぐ (oyogu)
書いて, 泳いで
書いた, 泳いだ
く → いて, ぐ → いで (Drop consonant, add い)
rows.note: CRITICAL EXCEPTION: 行く (iku) does NOT become いいて! It becomes 行って (itte) / 行った (itta)!

rows.label: Group 1: す
cells: 話す (hanasu), 出す (dasu)
話して, 出して
話した, 出した
す → して / した (Regular change)
rows.note: Behaves cleanly like polite shimasu.

rows.label: Group 2: る (Ichidan)
cells: 食べる (taberu), 見る (miru), 起きる (okiru)
食べて, 見て, 起きて
食べた, 見た, 起きた
Simply drop る and attach て / た
rows.note: Vowel before る is usually e or i (tabe-, mi-).

rows.label: Group 3: Irregular (変格)
cells: する (suru), 来る (kuru)
して, 来て (きて)
した, 来た (きた)
Completely irregular, mug up pronunciation of 来 (ki-te, ki-ta)!
rows.note: Notice 来る (kuru) changes reading to "ki" in て/た form!

sentences.japanese: すみませんが、窓を開けてください。
sentences.english: Excuse me, but please open the window.
sentences.literal: Excuse-me but, window open please.
sentences.nuanceNote: 開ける is Ru-verb: stem 開け + て + ください.

quiz.question: ここで写真を（　　）はいけません。撮影禁止です。
quiz.translation: You must not take photos here. Photography is prohibited.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜てはいけません prohibition
quiz.ruleHint: う・つ・る→って | む・ぶ・ぬ→んで | く→いて (行く→行って!) | ぐ→いで | す→して | る(一段)→て

explanations.reason: Correct! 撮る conjugates to 撮って + はいけません for strict prohibition.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot connect to はいけません.
Incorrect. Masu-stem cannot connect to はいけません.
Incorrect. Past form cannot connect to はいけません.

title: 〜ている (Actions in Progress vs Resulting Continuous States)
meaning: 1) Ongoing action occurring right now (eating, studying). 2) Continuous state resulting from a past change (married, living, knowing).
connection: V-て + いる / います
nuance: ている can describe an action in progress, a resulting state, or a repeated activity depending on the verb and context. 結婚している usually means is married; 住んでいる describes living somewhere. 知っている means know, and the ordinary negative answer is 知りません. This is the beginner default, not a prohibition against every contextual use of 知っていない. Do not assume that every verb with ている translates as English is doing.
keyTakeaway: Choose the meaning from the verb and context: ongoing action, resulting state, or repetition.

sentences.japanese: 姉は東京のIT企業に勤めています。
sentences.english: My older sister is employed at an IT company in Tokyo.
sentences.literal: Older-sister Tokyo IT-company-at employed-state-is.
sentences.nuanceNote: 勤めている indicates ongoing occupational employment state.

quiz.question: 田中さんの電話番号を（　　）か。「いいえ、知りません。」
quiz.translation: Do you know Tanaka-san's phone number? "No, I don't know."
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ている for state of knowledge
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + いる / います

explanations.reason: Correct! State of possessing information requires 知っています.
Incorrect. 知ります means "I will find out in the future".
Incorrect. Unnatural technical jargon.
Incorrect. 〜てある is only for deliberate actions on objects.

title: 〜んです / 〜のだ (The Explanatory Mode)
meaning: Provides background explanation, clarifies reasons, asks for clarification, or invites empathy: "The thing is... / You see..."
connection: Plain form + んです | な-adj / Noun + な + んです (Note the な!)
nuance: んです connects the statement to relevant background, an observed situation or a request for explanation. A plain factual statement such as 頭が痛いです is normal; it is not inherently cold or medical. 頭が痛いんです presents the headache as explanatory in context. Overusing んです can sound as if every statement requires justification, and んですか can sound probing. Nouns and な-adjectives use なんです only in their non-past affirmative form; past and negative forms keep their endings.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Noun / な-adj + [なんです] (NOT だんです ❌!).

sentences.japanese: どうして遅刻したのですか。「目覚まし時計が鳴らなかったんです。」
sentences.english: Why were you late? "The thing is, my alarm clock didn't ring."
sentences.literal: Why late-did? Alarm clock rang-not-explanatory.
sentences.nuanceNote: Explanatory んです provides the empathetic reason for the mishap.

quiz.question: 明日は大事な試験で（　　）んです。今夜は遊びに行けません。
quiz.translation: The thing is, I have a major exam tomorrow. I cannot go out to play tonight.
quiz.grammarFocus: い-adjective connection to んです
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + んです | な-adj / Noun + な + んです (Note the な!)

explanations.reason: Correct! Plain form 忙しい connects directly to んです.
Incorrect. い-adjectives never take だ.
Incorrect. Adverbial form cannot attach to んです.
Incorrect. な is only for な-adjectives and nouns.

title: 可能形 (Potential Verbs: Ability & Possibility)
meaning: Expresses that one can do something or that something is possible. Ru-verbs: drop る + られる | U-verbs: u-sound changes to e-sound + る.
chapter: Lesson 13: Looking for a Part-time Job
connection: Ru-verbs: 食べる→食べられる | U-verbs: 行く→行ける, 飲む→飲める, 話す→話せる | Irregular: する→できる, くる→こられる
nuance: PARTICLE SHIFT TRAP: When a transitive verb converts to potential form, the direct object particle を frequently shifts to が! 日本語を話す → 日本語が話せる (I can speak Japanese).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: U-verbs: u -> e + る (書く→書ける). The object particle を often becomes が!

sentences.japanese: 漢字が難しくて、新聞をすらすら読むことができません（読めません）。
sentences.english: The kanji are difficult, so I cannot read the newspaper smoothly.
sentences.literal: Kanji difficult-being, newspaper smoothly read cannot.
sentences.nuanceNote: 読む (U-verb) becomes 読める in potential form (読めません).

quiz.question: 刺身は新鮮ですが、どうしても生魚が（　　）。
quiz.translation: The sashimi is fresh, but I just cannot eat raw fish.
quiz.grammarFocus: 可能形 potential negative
quiz.ruleHint: Ru-verbs: 食べる→食べられる | U-verbs: 行く→行ける, 飲む→飲める, 話す→話せる | Irregular: する→できる, くる→こられる

explanations.reason: Correct! 食べる potential negative is 食べられない / 食べられません.
Incorrect. 食べません is a simple will decision ("I will not eat"), not ability.
Incorrect. Causative ("I will not let someone eat").
Incorrect. Favors pattern ("Cannot get someone to eat").

title: 〜ておく / 〜とく (Doing in Advance / Preparatory Action)
meaning: Performing an action in advance to prepare for future convenience or leaving a state as is for later.
connection: V-て + おく (Casual spoken contraction: 〜ておく → 〜とく / 〜でおく → 〜どく)
nuance: Forward-looking mindset: "I'll buy tickets beforehand so we don't wait in line" (切符を買っておく). In casual speech, 買っておく becomes 買っとく, 飲んでおく becomes 飲んどく.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-て + おく = Action done in advance for future convenience. Contracted: 〜とく.

sentences.japanese: パーティーの前に、部屋を綺麗に掃除しておきます。
sentences.english: Before the party, I will clean up the room nicely in advance.
sentences.literal: Party's before, room cleanly clean-up in-advance.
sentences.nuanceNote: Preparatory action executed specifically for the upcoming party.

quiz.question: 明日から旅行なので、ホテルの予約を（　　）おきました。
quiz.translation: Since I'm traveling from tomorrow, I made hotel reservations in advance.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ておく te-form connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + おく (Casual spoken contraction: 〜ておく → 〜とく / 〜でおく → 〜どく)

explanations.reason: Correct! する becomes して, forming しておきました ("reserved in advance").
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot connect to おく.
Incorrect. Past form cannot connect to おく.
Incorrect. Masu-stem cannot connect to おく.

title: 〜やすい vs 〜にくい (Easy to Do vs Difficult to Do)
meaning: Evaluates psychological or physical ease/difficulty of an action: 〜やすい (easy to do / prone to), 〜にくい (hard to do / resistant to).
connection: V-stem (ます形 without ます) + やすい / にくい (Conjugate as い-adjectives: 〜やすくない, 〜やすかった)
nuance: Once attached to the verb stem, the compound behaves 100% like a normal い-adjective! Also used for tendencies: このグラスは割れやすい (this glass breaks easily).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + やすい (Easy) / にくい (Hard). Functions grammatically as an い-adjective.

sentences.japanese: このペンは握りやすくて、長時間の筆記でも手が疲れません。
sentences.english: This pen is easy to grip, so my hand doesn't tire even during long periods of writing.
sentences.literal: This pen grip-easy and, long-time writing even hand tire-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Physical ergonomic ease (握る stem 握り + やすくて).

quiz.question: この本は字が大きくて、子供にもとても（　　）やすい。
quiz.translation: This book has large print, so it is very easy to read even for children.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜やすい verb stem connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます形 without ます) + やすい / にくい (Conjugate as い-adjectives: 〜やすくない, 〜やすかった)

explanations.reason: Correct! 読む stem is 読み, forming 読みやすい ("easy to read").
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach to やすい.
Incorrect. Te-stem cannot attach to やすい.
Incorrect. Negative stem cannot attach to やすい.

title: 〜時（とき） (When / At the time of)
meaning: When; at the time a situation holds or an event occurs.
connection: V-辞書形 + 時 (Before doing) / V-た + 時 (After doing) / い形 + 時 / な形 + な時 / N + の時
nuance: With a bounded action, dictionary-form とき commonly locates the main event before completion, while たとき commonly locates it after completion. Compare 日本へ行くとき買った and 日本へ行ったとき買った. This is a relative-time contrast, not a rule that every たとき refers to a finished event: 困ったとき means when in trouble, and 子供だったとき means when I was a child. Interpret tense together with the predicate's meaning and the surrounding situation.
keyTakeaway: Use relative timing and the type of situation; とき is not mechanically before versus after.

table.title: Time & Instant Sequence Spectrum (時・継起のグラデーション)
table.subtitle: How Japanese grammar sharpens from general timing to split-second interruption.

rows.label: 〜最中に (さいちゅうに)
cells: N3
Right in the middle of active ongoing action
Interrupted by unexpected outside event ❌
Main clause is ALWAYS an unexpected hindrance (電話が鳴った, 停電した).
rows.note: Conjugation: V-ている + 最中に / N の最中に

rows.label: 〜うちに
cells: N3
Within limited window before condition changes
Natural change or spontaneous urge ⚠️
Do it while hot / Before you forget (冷めないうちに / 忘れないうちに).
rows.note: Conjugation: V-dictionary / V-ない / Nの + うちに

rows.label: 〜たとたん（に）
cells: N3
The exact split-second after X finishes
Immediate surprise, NO speaker volition ❌
Clause B is a sudden surprise event (立ち上がったとたん、めまいがした).
rows.note: Conjugation: V-た + とたん（に）

rows.label: 〜かと思うと / 〜かと思ったら
cells: N2
Right when you thought X had occurred
Sharp unexpected contrast / sudden change ❌
Cannot describe speaker's deliberate action (空が暗くなったかと思うと、雨が降ってきた).
rows.note: Conjugation: V-た + かと思うと

rows.label: 〜か〜ないかのうちに
cells: N2
Literally on the border of completion
Simultaneous / instantaneous sequence
Almost no time gap: ベルが鳴り終わるか終わらないかのうちに.
rows.note: Conjugation: V-辞書形 / V-た + か + V-ない + かのうちに

rows.label: 〜次第 (しだい)
cells: N2
Immediate trigger for planned next step
HIGH speaker volition & business resolve ✅
Used for future events: 決まり次第、ご連絡いたします.
rows.note: Conjugation: V-stem + 次第 (NO past tense in main clause!)

sentences.japanese: 日本へ行く時、新しいカメラを買った。
sentences.english: When I was going to Japan, I bought a new camera.
sentences.literal: Japan toward go time, new camera bought.
sentences.nuanceNote: Notice 行く (dictionary form) is used: The camera was bought in his home country BEFORE departing for Japan!
sentences.trapAlert: If you say 行った時、カメラを買った, you bought the camera AFTER arriving in Japan.

sentences.japanese: 困った時は、いつでも遠慮なく連絡してください。
sentences.english: When you are in trouble, please contact me anytime without hesitation.
sentences.literal: Troubled time-as-for, anytime hesitation-without contact please.
sentences.nuanceNote: 困った is past/state: the trouble has already occurred when you reach out.

quiz.question: 旅行に行く（　　）、パスポートを確認しました。
quiz.translation: Before going on a trip, I checked my passport.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜時 tense sequencing before departure
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 + 時 (Before doing) / V-た + 時 (After doing) / い形 + 時 / な形 + な時 / N + の時

explanations.reason: 前に marks before the event.
前で would mark a physical action location, not this time relation.
前を does not connect this temporal clause.
前が cannot connect these clauses as written.

title: 〜ながら (While doing... simultaneous action)
meaning: Two actions performed simultaneously by the SAME person. Action B is the primary focus; Action A is secondary.
connection: V-stem (ます形 without ます) + ながら
nuance: For simultaneous actions, the same person performs both, and the final predicate presents the main action: 音楽を聞きながら勉強する. Do not use this simultaneous-action pattern for separate actors. Concessive ながら, as in 知っていながら, is a different use meaning although.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + ながら. Same subject only. The second clause is the MAIN action.

sentences.japanese: 音楽を聴きながら、毎朝漢字を復習しています。
sentences.english: While listening to music, I review kanji every morning.
sentences.literal: Music listening-while, every-morning kanji review am-doing.
sentences.nuanceNote: Kanji review is the main task; music listening is the secondary background action.

quiz.question: 彼はいつもコーヒーを（　　）ながら、仕事のメールをチェックしている。
quiz.translation: He is always checking work emails while drinking coffee.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ながら verb stem connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます形 without ます) + ながら

explanations.reason: Correct! 飲む stem is 飲み (飲みます without ます), forming 飲みながら.
Incorrect. Dictionary form 飲む cannot attach to ながら.
Incorrect. Te-form 飲んで does not take ながら (that would be redundant/ungrammatical).
Incorrect. Past form 飲んだ cannot connect to ながら.

title: 〜うちに (While... / Before condition changes)
meaning: 1) Do something while a favorable condition still lasts. 2) While X was going on, natural change Y spontaneously occurred.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-ている / V-ない + うちに | い形 + うちに | な形 + な + うちに | N + の + うちに
nuance: Unlike あいだ (neutral objective time span), うちに carries a subjective urgency: "If I don't do it now, the chance will vanish!" (e.g., while the soup is hot, before forgetting). With spontaneous changes, it marks an unnoticed gradual transition (e.g., while listening to lecture, I fell asleep).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-ないうちに = "Before [bad condition] happens!" (e.g. 暗くならないうちに = before it gets dark).

sentences.japanese: スープが温かいうちに、早く召し上がってください。
sentences.english: Please eat the soup quickly while it is still warm.
sentences.literal: Soup warm while, quickly enjoy-please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Urgency: Once it gets cold, the optimal state is lost.

sentences.japanese: 雨が降らないうちに、急いで洗濯物を取り込もう。
sentences.english: Let's hurry and bring in the laundry before it starts raining.
sentences.literal: Rain fall-not while, hurrying laundry take-in-volitional.
sentences.nuanceNote: 降らないうちに literally translates as "while it is not raining", which functionally means "before it starts raining".

quiz.question: 忘れない（　　）、先生が言った重要事項をメモしておいた。
quiz.translation: Before I forget, I took notes on the important points the teacher mentioned.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ないうちに (before [undesirable change] happens)
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-ている / V-ない + うちに | い形 + うちに | な形 + な + うちに | N + の + うちに

explanations.reason: Correct! 忘れないうちに means "while I haven't forgotten = before I forget". Perfect fit.
Incorrect. 最中に means "right in the middle of doing an active process" and cannot connect to negative 忘れない.
Incorrect. 次第 attaches to verb stems to mean "as soon as (future)", not negative states.
Incorrect. つつ attaches to verb stems for formal simultaneous action ("while doing").

title: 〜最中に（さいちゅうに） (Right in the middle of... disrupted!)
meaning: Right in the middle of an ongoing activity.
connection: V-ている + 最中に / N + の最中に
nuance: 最中 means right in the middle of an activity. An unexpected interruption often follows 最中に, but interruption is a common context, not an obligatory part of its meaning.
keyTakeaway: 最中 means right in the middle of an activity. An unexpected interruption often follows 最中に, but interruption is a common context, not an obligatory part of its meaning.

sentences.japanese: 大切な会議の最中に、スマートフォンの着信音が鳴り響いて焦った。
sentences.english: Right in the middle of an important meeting, my smartphone ringtone rang loudly and I panicked.
sentences.literal: Important meeting's midst-in, smartphone ringtone echoed and panicked.
sentences.nuanceNote: Notice the sudden embarrassing disruption (ringtone sounding during a meeting).

quiz.question: シャワーを（　　）最中に、突然停電になって真っ暗になった。
quiz.translation: Right in the middle of taking a shower, the power suddenly went out and it became pitch dark.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜最中に connection to ongoing action
quiz.ruleHint: V-ている + 最中に / N + の最中に

explanations.reason: Correct! V-ている form represents the ongoing state that gets disrupted by the sudden blackout.
Incorrect. 浴びた is past completed form. You cannot be in the middle of an action that is already finished.
Incorrect. Dictionary form 浴びる cannot attach directly to 最中に.
Incorrect. 浴びようとする means "about to take a shower", which doesn't match the ongoing action meaning of 最中.

title: 〜たとたん（に） (The moment that... sudden surprise)
meaning: The instant action A took place, unexpected event B immediately occurred.
connection: V-た + とたん（に）
nuance: Crucial JLPT rule: Clause B is ALWAYS a surprise or natural reflexive reaction! It CANNOT be a planned, intentional, or volitional command (e.g. you CANNOT say "窓を開けたとたん、掃除してください" ❌).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-た + とたんに + [UNEXPECTED event]. Zero speaker volition allowed.

sentences.japanese: 立ち上がったとたんに、激しいめまいがして倒れそうになった。
sentences.english: The moment I stood up, I felt severe dizziness and almost collapsed.
sentences.literal: Stood-up moment-at, severe dizziness did and almost-fell became.
sentences.nuanceNote: A classic physiological surprise reaction: instant trigger -> involuntary reaction.

quiz.question: 薬を（　　）とたん、猛烈な眠気に襲われてベッドに倒れ込んだ。
quiz.translation: The moment I took the medicine, I was struck by violent drowsiness and collapsed into bed.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜たとたん verb form restriction
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + とたん（に）

explanations.reason: Correct! V-た + とたん forms 飲んだとたん ("the moment after I swallowed it").
Incorrect. Dictionary form 飲む cannot attach to とたん.
Incorrect. Continuous form 飲んでいる cannot attach to とたん (that would be 最中).
Incorrect. Volitional form 飲もう does not connect to とたん.

title: 〜（か）と思うと / 〜かと思ったら (No sooner had... when suddenly!)
meaning: No sooner had X happened than event Y immediately followed, presenting a striking or contradictory change.
connection: V-た + （か）と思うと / 〜かと思ったら
nuance: Expresses the speaker's astonishment at a rapid transition or contradictory shift. Often describes weather, crying/laughing children, or rapid departures. Cannot describe the speaker's own planned deliberate action!
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-た + かと思うと = "Just when you thought it finished, BAM! Complete opposite/sudden change."

sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんはさっきまで泣いていたかと思うと、もうすやすや眠っている。
sentences.english: Just when I thought the baby was crying until a moment ago, she is already sleeping peacefully.
sentences.literal: Baby until-moment-ago crying-was thought-if, already peacefully sleeping.
sentences.nuanceNote: Contrasting swift change in state: crying -> sound asleep in an instant.

tokens.meaning: no sooner than / just when thought

quiz.question: 空が急に暗くなった（　　）、雷とともに大粒の雨が降ってきた。
quiz.translation: No sooner had the sky suddenly darkened than large drops of rain came pouring down with thunder.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜かと思うと sudden rapid weather shift
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + （か）と思うと / 〜かと思ったら

explanations.reason: Correct! V-た + かと思うと captures the astonishingly fast transition from darkening sky to downpour.
Incorrect. 次第 attaches to verb stems to mean "as soon as (business future)", not past weather observations.
Incorrect. ながら requires verb stem and indicates simultaneous actions by the same agent.
Incorrect. 一方だ means "keeps trending in one continuous direction", not an instantaneous occurrence.

title: 〜か〜ないかのうちに (On the very verge of... / Barely finished when)
meaning: Describes an event occurring with virtually ZERO time interval—so fast that you cannot even tell if the first action finished.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-た + か + V-ない + かのうちに (The two verbs are the EXACT same verb!)
nuance: The ultimate Japanese expression for split-second succession. Uses the same verb twice: 終わるか終わらないかのうちに ("in the space between whether it ended or didn't end"). Highly literary and dramatic.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Verb] + か + [Verb-ない] + かのうちに. Identical verb in affirmative and negative.

sentences.japanese: 授業終了のチャイムが鳴り終わるか終わらないかのうちに、生徒たちは教室を飛び出した。
sentences.english: Hardly had the class chime finished ringing when the students dashed out of the classroom.
sentences.literal: Class finish chime ring-finish or ring-finish-not interval-in, students classroom dashed-out.
sentences.nuanceNote: Notice the extreme immediacy: chime was barely fading and students were already running.

tokens.reading: じゅぎょうしゅうりょう

tokens.word: 鳴り終わるか終わらないかのうちに
tokens.reading: なりおわるかおわらないかのうちに
tokens.romaji: nariowaru ka owaranai ka no uchi ni

quiz.question: 布団に横たわるか（　　）かのうちに、深い眠りに落ちてしまった。
quiz.translation: Hardly had I laid down on the futon when I fell into a deep sleep.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜か〜ないかのうちに parallel verb pattern
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-た + か + V-ない + かのうちに (The two verbs are the EXACT same verb!)

explanations.reason: Correct! The formula is V-辞書形 (横たわる) + か + V-ない (横たわらない) + かのうちに.
Incorrect. The second slot requires the negative form, not past affirmative.
Incorrect. Masu-stem cannot be placed in the negative slot.
Incorrect. You cannot duplicate the affirmative form without negative contrast.

title: 〜次第（しだい） (As soon as... business resolve)
meaning: As soon as action A is completed or verified in the future, action B will immediately be executed.
connection: V-stem (ます形 without ます) + 次第
nuance: Essential business Japanese! The main clause expresses the speaker's intentional future action, commitment, or request. CRITICAL JLPT TRAP: The main clause can NEVER be in the past tense (た)! If it's already in the past, use 〜たら or 〜とたん.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-stem + 次第 + [FUTURE resolve/request]. Never past tense!

sentences.japanese: 詳しい日程が決まり次第、担当者よりメールにてご連絡いたします。
sentences.english: As soon as the detailed schedule is finalized, our representative will contact you via email.
sentences.literal: Detailed schedule decide-as-soon-as, person-in-charge from email via contact will-do.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite business commitment regarding a future milestone.

tokens.reading: ごれんらくいたします

quiz.question: パスポートの準備が（　　）次第、旅行会社に書類を提出してください。
quiz.translation: As soon as your passport preparation is complete, please submit the documents to the travel agency.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜次第 verb stem connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-stem (ます形 without ます) + 次第

explanations.reason: Correct! できる stem is でき (できます without ます), forming でき次第.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot attach directly to 次第 in this time pattern.
Incorrect. Past form できた cannot attach to 次第.
Incorrect. Progressive form does not attach to 次第.

title: 〜から vs 〜ので (Reasons & Background)
meaning: Both give reasons; ので often presents background more gently, while から readily supports the speaker's decision.
connection: 〜から: Plain/Polite form + から | 〜ので: Verb/い形 plain + ので / な形 + なので / N + なので
nuance: Both から and ので give reasons. ので often presents a circumstance more gently and can precede a polite request or invitation. から readily states the speaker's reason for a decision. Register, context and the strength of the request matter; requests do not universally require から.
keyTakeaway: Both から and ので give reasons. ので often presents a circumstance more gently and can precede a polite request or invitation. から readily states the speaker's reason for a decision. Register, context and the strength of the request matter; requests do not universally require から.

sentences.japanese: 危ないですから、黄色い線の内側にお下がりください。
sentences.english: Because it is dangerous, please step back behind the yellow line.
sentences.literal: Dangerous is because, yellow line's inside-to step-back please.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite station announcement with direct request/instruction to passengers.

quiz.question: 明日は大事な試験が（　　）から、今夜は早く寝ようと思う。
quiz.translation: Because I have an important exam tomorrow, I think I will go to bed early tonight.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜から plain form connection
quiz.ruleHint: 〜から: Plain/Polite form + から | 〜ので: Verb/い形 plain + ので / な形 + なので / N + なので

explanations.reason: Correct! Plain non-past ある connects cleanly to から.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot connect directly to から.
Incorrect. Stem form あり is ungrammatical before から.
Incorrect. Volitional form cannot be used as the factual condition here.

title: 〜てしまう / 〜ちゃう (Irreversible Completion & Regret)
meaning: 1) Completely finished doing something to the end. 2) Done by accident or mistake with deep regret ("Oh no, I did it!").
connection: V-て + しまう (Spoken contractions: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう / 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう)
nuance: Crucial dual nature: Sometimes it means proud complete accomplishment (本を全部読んでしまった = I read the whole book!), but overwhelmingly on JLPT tests it signifies unintentional mistake and regret (財布を落としてしまった = I lost my wallet, alas).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-てしまう = Complete finish OR irreversible regret. Contracted: 忘れちゃった!

sentences.japanese: 電車の網棚に大切な書類の入ったバッグを忘れてしまった。
sentences.english: I accidentally left my bag with important documents on the train's luggage rack.
sentences.literal: Train luggage-rack on important documents entered bag forgot-regretfully.
sentences.nuanceNote: Deep remorse and frustration over an irreversible blunder.

quiz.question: 急いでいたので、違う色の靴下を（　　）しまった。
quiz.translation: Because I was in a hurry, I ended up putting on different-colored socks by mistake.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜てしまう te-form connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + しまう (Spoken contractions: 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう / 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう)

explanations.reason: Correct! 履く (to wear shoes/socks) becomes 履いて in te-form, forming 履いてしまった.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot connect to しまう.
Incorrect. Masu-stem 履き does not connect to しまう.
Incorrect. Past form 履いた cannot precede しまう.

title: 〜おかげで vs 〜せいで (Gratitude vs Blame)
meaning: 〜おかげで: Thanks to X, a good outcome Y resulted. 〜せいで: Because of X (blaming X), a terrible outcome Y resulted.
connection: Plain form (V / い形) + おかげで / せいで | な形 + な + おかげで / せいで | N + の + おかげで / せいで
nuance: Irony note: Sometimes おかげで is used sarcastically ("Thanks to your terrible driving, we are lost"), but on the JLPT, treat おかげで as POSITIVE and せいで as NEGATIVE BLAME! You can also end a sentence with 〜せいだ / 〜おかげだ.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: おかげで = Gratitude (Positive). せいで = Blame (Negative). Noun + の + おかげ/せい.

sentences.japanese: 先生の熱心なご指導のおかげで、無事に合格することができました。
sentences.english: Thanks to the teacher's enthusiastic guidance, I was able to pass safely.
sentences.literal: Teacher's enthusiastic guidance's thanks-to, safely pass doing was-able-to.
sentences.nuanceNote: Expresses genuine gratitude towards a benefactor.

tokens.word: 合格することができました
tokens.reading: ごうかくすることができました

sentences.japanese: 台風のせいで、楽しみにしていた週末の花火大会が中止になってしまった。
sentences.english: Because of the typhoon, the weekend fireworks festival I was looking forward to got cancelled.
sentences.literal: Typhoon's fault-because, looking-forward-was weekend fireworks festival cancellation became-regretfully.
sentences.nuanceNote: Blaming the typhoon for ruining anticipated plans.

tokens.word: 中止になってしまった
tokens.reading: ちゅうしになってしまった

quiz.question: 隣の部屋の騒音の（　　）、昨夜は一睡もできなかった。
quiz.translation: Because of the noise from the next room, I couldn't sleep a wink last night.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜せいで negative blame attribution
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form (V / い形) + おかげで / せいで | な形 + な + おかげで / せいで | N + の + おかげで / せいで

explanations.reason: せいで marks the blamed cause.
を would need a different following predicate.
せいに requires a construction such as せいにする.
と does not link this cause to the result.

title: 〜ばかりに (Simply because of... a catastrophic outcome)
meaning: Simply because of that one single thing / trivial action, an unexpectedly terrible, disastrous result happened.
connection: V-た / い形 / な形-な / N-である + ばかりに
nuance: Expresses deep bite-your-tongue regret and frustration: "If only I hadn't done that one little thing, this catastrophe wouldn't have occurred!" The result clause is ALWAYS negative, tragic, or disadvantageous.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: V-た + ばかりに + [DISASTROUS OUTCOME]. Pure remorse.

sentences.japanese: 嘘をついたばかりに、親友からの信頼を完全に失ってしまった。
sentences.english: Simply because I told a lie, I completely lost the trust of my best friend.
sentences.literal: Lie told simply-because, best-friend from trust completely lost-regretfully.
sentences.nuanceNote: One lie (trivial action) spiraled into complete loss of friendship (disaster).

quiz.question: 道を一本（　　）ばかりに、飛行機の出発時刻に間に合わなかった。
quiz.translation: Simply because I took one wrong turn, I failed to make the flight's departure time.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ばかりに past tense connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-た / い形 / な形-な / N-である + ばかりに

explanations.reason: Correct! V-た (間違えた) + ばかりに highlights the single mistake that triggered missing the plane.
Incorrect. Non-past dictionary form is rare and does not fit a past missed flight.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot attach directly to ばかりに.
Incorrect. 〜そう (looks like) does not connect to ばかりに.

title: 〜ものだから / 〜もので (Social Excuse / "It couldn't be helped")
meaning: Giving a personal explanation or mild excuse to justify why you were late, couldn't attend, or failed to do something.
connection: Plain form + ものだから / もので | な形 + な + ものだから | N + な + ものだから
nuance: Subtle psychology: It appeals to the listener's empathy! "The circumstances were such that any reasonable person would have done the same." In casual conversation, contracted to 〜もんだから or simply 〜もん (childish/informal excuse).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Circumstance] + なものだから = "Please forgive me, it was unavoidable circumstances!"

sentences.japanese: 途中で事故渋滞に巻き込まれたものだから、集合時間に遅れてしまいました。
sentences.english: Because I got caught in an accident traffic jam on the way, I unfortunately ended up late for the meeting time.
sentences.literal: On-the-way accident congestion in wrapped-was because, gathering time to was-late.
sentences.nuanceNote: Polite, empathetic excuse explaining an unavoidable delay.

tokens.reading: おくれてしまいました

quiz.question: あまりに（　　）ものだから、ついダイエット中なのにケーキを食べてしまった。
quiz.translation: Because it looked so utterly delicious, I ended up eating cake even though I was in the middle of a diet.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ものだから justification for temptation
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form + ものだから / もので | な形 + な + ものだから | N + な + ものだから

explanations.reason: Correct! "Because it looked so delicious" explains the uncontrollable urge to eat the cake.
Incorrect. You hadn't tasted it yet; it was the visual appeal (そう) that tempted you.
Incorrect. Needs past tense or proper connective な before もの.
Incorrect. Focusing on past taste fails to explain the initial temptation.

title: 〜からには / 〜以上（は） (Now that... I must naturally / Resolute commitment)
meaning: Now that situation X has become reality, it is only natural, proper, and obligatory that course Y must follow.
connection: Plain form (V / い形 / な形である / Nである) + からには / 以上（は）
nuance: Strong moral conviction and determination! The second clause almost ALWAYS ends in volition, necessity, or command: 〜つもりだ, 〜べきだ, 〜なければならない, or 〜てください. Never used for passive accidental results.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: 〜からには + [強い意志・義務・覚悟] (つもリだ、べきだ、〜てみせる).

sentences.japanese: JLPT N2を受験すると決めたからには、最後まで諦めずに全力で勉強するつもりだ。
sentences.english: Now that I have decided to take the JLPT N2, I intend to study with all my might until the very end without giving up.
sentences.literal: JLPT N2 take-exam that decided now-that, last until not-giving-up full-power study intend.
sentences.nuanceNote: Unwavering resolve and personal accountability following a commitment.

tokens.reading: べんきょうするつもりだ

quiz.question: 一度引き受けた（　　）、どんなに困難でも責任を持ってやり遂げるべきだ。
quiz.translation: Now that you have accepted the task, no matter how difficult it is, you ought to see it through with responsibility.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜からには moral duty and resolve
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form (V / い形 / な形である / Nである) + からには / 以上（は）

explanations.reason: Correct! "Now that you took on the job, you must finish it" is the signature meaning of からには.
Incorrect. あまり means "due to excessive emotion/stress, an abnormal result occurred".
Incorrect. あげく means "after a long struggle, ended up with a bad result".
Incorrect. 末に means "after a long process, a decision was reached", without the moral command tone.

title: 〜あまり (Excessive emotion leading to abnormal outcome)
meaning: Because an emotion, stress, or excitement was so overwhelming and extreme, an abnormal, unusual, or out-of-control result occurred.
connection: V-辞書形 / V-た + あまり | N + の + あまり
nuance: あまり expresses an excessive feeling, action or degree that leads to a result. Emotional causes are common, but it is not restricted to psychological states or catastrophic outcomes.
keyTakeaway: あまり expresses an excessive feeling, action or degree that leads to a result. Emotional causes are common, but it is not restricted to psychological states or catastrophic outcomes.

sentences.japanese: 面接の際、極度の緊張のあまり、用意していた自己紹介の言葉が全部飛んでしまった。
sentences.english: During the interview, out of extreme nervousness, the self-introduction words I had prepared completely vanished from my mind.
sentences.literal: Interview occasion-at, extreme nervousness's excess-at, prepared self-intro words all flew-regretfully.
sentences.nuanceNote: Paralyzing stress causing mind to go completely blank.

quiz.question: 母は私の合格通知を見て、嬉しさの（　　）大声を上げて泣き崩れた。
quiz.translation: Seeing my acceptance letter, my mother broke down in tears and shouted out of sheer joy.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜あまり emotional overload outcome
quiz.ruleHint: V-辞書形 / V-た + あまり | N + の + あまり

explanations.reason: Correct! 嬉しさのあまり expresses joy so intense that it caused her to cry uncontrollably.
Incorrect. おかげで explains logical gratitude, not an involuntary psychological reflex.
Incorrect. せいで implies blame for a bad thing, but acceptance is a wonderful event.
Incorrect. 次第 means "as soon as (business)" and cannot connect to an emotion noun in this way.

title: 〜あげく / 〜あげくに (After prolonged ordeal... ended up with a bad result)
meaning: After undergoing a prolonged process of agonizing, arguing, or struggling, the final outcome was unfortunately bad or wasted effort.
connection: V-た + あげく / N + の + あげく
nuance: あげく presents a result after a process, often with an unwanted or disappointing outcome. 末に can introduce either a favorable or unfavorable conclusion after a process.
keyTakeaway: あげく presents a result after a process, often with an unwanted or disappointing outcome. 末に can introduce either a favorable or unfavorable conclusion after a process.

sentences.japanese: 何時間も迷いに迷ったあげく、結局何も買わずに店を出てしまった。
sentences.english: After hesitating and agonizing for hours, in the end I left the store without buying anything.
sentences.literal: Many-hours agonizing-agonized end-in, eventually nothing buying-without store exited-regretfully.
sentences.nuanceNote: Huge expenditure of time and mental energy with zero fruit to show for it.

quiz.question: 夫婦で散々（　　）あげく、結局離婚することになってしまった。
quiz.translation: After arguing endlessly as husband and wife, in the end they unfortunately ended up getting divorced.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜あげく past tense connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-た + あげく / N + の + あげく

explanations.reason: Correct! V-た (口論した) + あげく accurately highlights the prolonged arguing that concluded in divorce.
Incorrect. Dictionary form cannot connect to あげく when describing a completed history.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot connect to あげく.
Incorrect. Volitional form does not fit.

title: The 4 Conditionals Decoded: と vs ば vs たら vs なら
meaning: Foundational N5/N4 conditionals that test learners continuously through N3 and N2: natural consequence (と), hypothetical requirement (ば), temporal trigger (たら), and contextual advice (なら).
connection: V-る + と | V-eば | V-た + ら | N / Plain + なら
nuance: と and ば are not freely interchangeable with たら and なら. In hypothetical action sequences, と normally does not introduce the speaker's request or volition. With ば, compatibility also depends on whether the first predicate is stative/negative and on the subjects. たら is versatile for after-completion requests; なら takes up a premise.
keyTakeaway: と and ば are not freely interchangeable with たら and なら. In hypothetical action sequences, と normally does not introduce the speaker's request or volition. With ば, compatibility also depends on whether the first predicate is stative/negative and on the subjects. たら is versatile for after-completion requests; なら takes up a premise.

table.title: The 4 Great Conditionals Decoded: と vs ば vs たら vs なら
table.subtitle: The #1 JLPT trap point across N4, N3, and N2. Never confuse them again.

rows.label: 〜と (Natural / Mechanic)
cells: Natural law, physics, mechanical trigger: "Once X happens, Y automatically follows."
STRICT NO ❌ (Never use ください, ましょう, つもりだ)
YES ✅ (Discovered a new surprise: 窓を開けると、雪が降っていた)
TRAP: If sentence ends in "〜てください", 〜と is IMMEDIATELY WRONG! Use 〜たら instead.
rows.note: Example: ボタンを押すと、切符が出る (Press button -> ticket dispenses).

rows.label: 〜ば (Provisional Hypothetical)
cells: Logical requirement: "Provided that X is met, Y is true."
RESTRICTED ⚠️ (Only if verb is non-action / state like ある, or subjects differ)
NO ❌ (Cannot express past surprise or single actual event)
TRAP: "薬を飲めば、熱が下がった" is WRONG. Use 飲んだら.
rows.note: Classic saying: 安ければ買う (If it is cheap, I will buy it).

rows.label: 〜たら (Chronological Trigger)
cells: "Once X is completed, THEN Y happens." The most versatile conditional.
YES ✅ (Freely allows requests, intentions, invitations: 〜てください, 〜ましょう)
YES ✅ (Indicates sequential discovery in the past: 家に帰ったら、手紙があった)
SAFE HARBOR: When in doubt on volitional clauses or conversational requests, たら is king.
rows.note: Connection: Past short form (た) + ら.

rows.label: 〜なら (Contextual Topic / Advice)
cells: "If that is the case you are talking about..." Topic conditional based on listener input.
YES ✅ (Excellent for advice, recommendations: 〜がいいですよ)
NO ❌ (Cannot be used for past factual sequences)
TRAP: Time inversion! In "日本へ行くなら、カメラを買ったほうがいい", you buy the camera BEFORE going!
rows.note: Noun / Plain form + なら (no だ).

sentences.japanese: この交差点を右に曲がると、左手に郵便局が見えます。
sentences.english: When you turn right at this intersection, you will see the post office on your left.
sentences.literal: This intersection right turn-if, left-hand-to post-office is-visible.
sentences.nuanceNote: Natural, automatic spatial consequence: turning the corner mechanically reveals the post office.

sentences.japanese: 京都へ行くなら、秋の紅葉の季節が一番おすすめですよ。
sentences.english: If you are going to Kyoto, the autumn foliage season is definitely the best recommendation.
sentences.literal: Kyoto to go if-case, autumn's red-leaves season number-one recommendation is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Listener brought up Kyoto; speaker provides expert situational advice with なら.

quiz.question: 駅に着い（　　）、すぐに私に電話をかけてください。
quiz.translation: When you arrive at the station, please give me a call immediately.
quiz.grammarFocus: Conditional permission with volitional command clause
quiz.ruleHint: V-る + と | V-eば | V-た + ら | N / Plain + なら

explanations.reason: Correct! 〜たら (着いたら) is the only conditional form here that naturally permits a polite command (〜てください) in the following clause.
Incorrect. Ungrammatical connection.
Incorrect. 着けば cannot pair with a volitional request when the same person controls the arrival.
Incorrect. 着くなら would mean "If you intend to arrive (before arriving)", but you want them to call AFTER arriving.

title: 〜さえ〜ば (If only X... then everything is fine)
meaning: If only one single essential condition X is fulfilled, everything else will naturally resolve and be satisfactory.
connection: N + さえ + V-ば / い形-ければ / な形-なら / N-なら | V-stem + さえすれば
nuance: Expresses minimalism and laser focus: all other concerns are trivial if this one condition is met. Highly frequent in JLPT reading passages (e.g., as long as you have health, as long as you love each other).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: N + さえ + [Conditional ば]. (e.g. 体さえ健康なら / 時間さえあれば).

sentences.japanese: どんなに辛い時でも、あなたさえそばにいてくれれば、私は乗り越えられます。
sentences.english: No matter how bitter the times, if only you are by my side, I can overcome anything.
sentences.literal: How-much bitter time even, you-only side-at being-give-if, I overcome can.
sentences.nuanceNote: Your presence alone is the one indispensable prerequisite.

quiz.question: お金（　　）あれば、幸せになれるというわけではない。
quiz.translation: It doesn't necessarily mean that you will become happy if only you have money.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜さえ〜ば minimal prerequisite marker
quiz.ruleHint: N + さえ + V-ば / い形-ければ / な形-なら / N-なら | V-stem + さえすれば

explanations.reason: Correct! お金さえあれば forms "if only one has money", perfectly completing the conditional.
Incorrect. こそ is for strong emphasis ("precisely because X") and doesn't form this conditional idiom.
Incorrect. お金ばかりあれば is ungrammatical.
Incorrect. ほど indicates degree or comparison ("to the extent of").

title: 〜としたら / 〜とすれば (Supposing that... / Pure hypothesis)
meaning: Setting up a hypothetical assumption or scenario: "If we suppose that X were true, then Y would follow."
connection: Plain form (V / い形 / な形だ / Nだ) + としたら / とすれば
nuance: Introduces imaginative, counter-factual, or thought-experiment conditions ("If you won 100 million yen...", "If aliens existed..."). としたら tends to focus on the speaker's subjective feelings or actions; とすれば focuses on logical deduction.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Plain form + としたら = "Suppose for a moment that X were reality..."

sentences.japanese: もし明日地球が滅亡するとしたら、あなたは何を食べたいですか。
sentences.english: Supposing that the earth were to be destroyed tomorrow, what would you want to eat?
sentences.literal: If tomorrow earth perish-if-suppose, you what eat-want?
sentences.nuanceNote: Pure fantasy thought experiment scenario.

tokens.reading: めつぼうするとしたら

quiz.question: その話が本当だ（　　）、大変な大事件になりますね。
quiz.translation: Supposing that story is true, it would become a massive incident, wouldn't it?
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜とすれば logical hypothesis deduction
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form (V / い形 / な形だ / Nだ) + としたら / とすれば

explanations.reason: Correct! Noun + だとすれば sets up the hypothesis: "If that premise holds, then logically Y follows".
Incorrect. にしたがって means "as X progresses, Y changes proportionately".
Incorrect. につれて denotes parallel continuous change over time.
Incorrect. とともに means "together with" or "simultaneously as".

title: 〜ものなら (If by any miracle it were possible / Threatening warning)
meaning: 1) If by some near-impossible miracle it could be done, I would love to! 2) If you dare make that one mistake, terrible consequences will follow.
connection: 1) V-可能形 (Potential) + ものなら | 2) V-意向形 / V-る + ものなら
nuance: With Potential verbs (やり直せるものなら, 帰れるものなら), it conveys heartbreaking longing for something virtually impossible in reality. With non-potential verbs (遅刻しようものなら), it carries a grave warning: "If you dare do X, you will face severe wrath!"
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Potential verb + ものなら = "If only it were remotely possible (alas it is not)".

sentences.japanese: 過去の過ちをやり直せるものなら、人生をもう一度最初からやり直したい。
sentences.english: If by any miracle I could redo my past mistakes, I would want to live my life over again from the beginning.
sentences.literal: Past mistakes redo-can-if-miracle, life once-more beginning from redo want.
sentences.nuanceNote: Deep, poignant longing acknowledging the impossibility of turning back time.

tokens.reading: やりなおせるものなら
tokens.meaning: if by any miracle I could redo

quiz.question: あの厳格な部長の前でミスを（　　）ものなら、即座に大目玉を食らうだろう。
quiz.translation: If you dare make a mistake in front of that strict general manager, you'll immediately get a furious scolding.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜（よ）うものなら warning conditional
quiz.ruleHint: 1) V-可能形 (Potential) + ものなら | 2) V-意向形 / V-る + ものなら

explanations.reason: Correct! V-よう (しよう) + ものなら expresses the ominous threat: "If you so much as dare make a mistake..."
Incorrect. Dictionary form without potential does not create this warning construction.
Incorrect. Past form した does not connect to ものなら.
Incorrect. Te-form cannot connect to ものなら.

title: 〜ないことには（〜ない） (Unless X happens... Y is impossible)
meaning: Unless condition X occurs first, result Y can fundamentally never happen or be determined.
connection: V-ない + ことには | い形-くない + ことには | な形-でない + ことには | N-でない + ことには
nuance: The result clause ALWAYS contains a negative or impossible predicate: 〜ない, 〜できない, 〜わからない. It establishes X as a strict, non-negotiable prerequisite gatekeeper.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [A-ないことには] + [B-できない / 分からない]. No X, no Y.

sentences.japanese: 実際に現場の状況を見てみないことには、正確な修理費用は見積もれない。
sentences.english: Unless we actually go and inspect the on-site situation, we cannot estimate the exact repair cost.
sentences.literal: Actually site's situation inspect-not unless, accurate repair cost estimate-cannot.
sentences.nuanceNote: Site inspection is an absolute prerequisite before an estimate can be provided.

tokens.nuance: Negative of 見てみる + ことには

quiz.question: 双方の話を直接（　　）ことには、どちらに責任があるか判断できない。
quiz.translation: Unless we listen directly to both sides' accounts, we cannot judge who bears the responsibility.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ないことには negative prerequisite connection
quiz.ruleHint: V-ない + ことには | い形-くない + ことには | な形-でない + ことには | N-でない + ことには

explanations.reason: Correct! V-ない (聞かない) + ことには forms "unless we listen... we cannot judge".
Incorrect. Past form cannot connect to ことには.
Incorrect. Affirmative dictionary form cannot connect here.
Incorrect. Progressive form cannot connect to ことには.

title: 〜だけ vs 〜しか〜ない (Limitation & Exclusion)
meaning: だけ limits the amount or scope; しか…ない excludes alternatives.
connection: Nだけ; Nしか + negative predicate; にだけ / にしか, でだけ / でしか
nuance: だけ can occur with either an affirmative or negative predicate. In the basic exclusion pattern, しか pairs with a negative predicate: 千円しかありません. It often implies that the amount is small, but dissatisfaction or insufficiency is not required: あなたにしかできない can praise someone's unique ability. しか normally replaces を/が, while particles such as に/で remain before it. Compare 読むだけ (only read) with 読むしかない (have no choice but to read).
keyTakeaway: しか requires a negative predicate in this construction; it does not always express dissatisfaction.

sentences.japanese: 財布の中に小銭が百円しか残っていない。
sentences.english: There is only a mere 100 yen in small change left in my wallet.
sentences.literal: Wallet inside small-change 100-yen only remaining-is-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Speaker laments having almost no money left (strong sense of insufficiency).

quiz.question: 「千円だけ持っています」と同じ金額を表します。千円（　　）持っていません。
quiz.translation: Express the same amount as I have only one thousand yen.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜しか〜ない negative agreement
quiz.ruleHint: Nだけ; Nしか + negative predicate; にだけ / にしか, でだけ / でしか

explanations.reason: しか with a negative predicate expresses only one thousand yen.
だけを with this negative would deny holding that particular amount rather than say it is all one has.
だけが cannot mark the possessed object of 持つ here.
だけに is not the object/exclusion construction needed here.

title: 〜をはじめ（として） (Starting with... primary representative)
meaning: Singling out the most prominent, representative example from a group, followed by many other similar items: "Starting with X, as well as many others."
connection: N + をはじめ / をはじめとして / をはじめとする + N
nuance: Formal and informative. Used when presenting an impressive lineup, delegation, or category where X is the flagship example (e.g. "Starting with the Prime Minister, many dignitaries attended").
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Flagship Noun] + をはじめ(として) + [全体・多くの人々].

sentences.japanese: 富士山をはじめ、日本には世界的に有名な観光名所が数多く存在している。
sentences.english: Starting with Mt. Fuji, numerous world-famous tourist attractions exist in Japan.
sentences.literal: Mt. Fuji starting-with, Japan-in globally famous tourist-spots many exist.
sentences.nuanceNote: Mt. Fuji represents the premier icon among Japan's numerous famous attractions.

quiz.question: 校長先生（　　）、教職員の皆様には心より感謝申し上げます。
quiz.translation: Starting with the Principal, I extend my heartfelt gratitude to all the faculty and staff.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜をはじめ representative leader introduction
quiz.ruleHint: N + をはじめ / をはじめとして / をはじめとする + N

explanations.reason: Correct! 校長先生をはじめ highlights the principal as the flagship leader of the entire teaching staff.
Incorrect. を通じて means "throughout a whole period" or "via a medium".
Incorrect. にわたって denotes continuous span across time or geographical space.
Incorrect. に限って means "of all unfortunate days" or "specifically only X".

title: 〜にわたって / 〜にわたり (Spanning across time or space)
meaning: An action, state, or phenomenon extends continuously across an entire expansive span of time, area, or scope.
connection: N (Time duration / Geographical expanse / Number of times) + にわたって / にわたり / にわたる + N
nuance: Signifies breadth, grand scale, and extensive duration (e.g., across 10 years, across the whole country, across 5 rounds of negotiations). It elevates the sense of scale compared to simple 間.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [大規模な時間・場所・回数] + にわたって (e.g. 10年間にわたる研究).

sentences.japanese: ３日間にわたる激しい議論の末に、ついに合意に達した。
sentences.english: After fierce debates spanning three full days, an agreement was finally reached.
sentences.literal: 3-days-span fierce debates end-at, finally agreement reached.
sentences.nuanceNote: Emphasizes the intense, exhausting continuous duration of three whole days.

quiz.question: 台風の影響で、関東全域（　　）停電が発生した。
quiz.translation: Due to the impact of the typhoon, power outages occurred spanning the entire Kanto region.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜にわたって geographical expanse
quiz.ruleHint: N (Time duration / Geographical expanse / Number of times) + にわたって / にわたり / にわたる + N

explanations.reason: Correct! 関東全域にわたって captures the vast geographic expanse over which blackouts occurred.
Incorrect. をはじめ requires a single representative member, not an entire region.
Incorrect. にとって means "from the perspective of".
Incorrect. をめぐって means "controversy surrounding a disputed issue".

title: 〜を通じて / 〜を通して (Throughout period / Via medium)
meaning: 1) Continuously throughout an entire uninterrupted period. 2) Doing or achieving something by means of / through an intermediary or medium.
connection: N + を通じて / を通して (つうじて / とおして)
nuance: Dual meaning: 1) Time: 四季を通じて (throughout the 4 seasons / all year round). 2) Medium: 友人を通じて知り合った (we got to know each other through a mutual friend). Note: Direct physical tools like pen/scissors take で, not を通じて.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: 1) 一年を通じて = All year round. 2) インターネットを通じて = Via the internet.

sentences.japanese: この地域は温暖で、一年を通じて様々なフルーツが栽培されている。
sentences.english: This region has a mild climate, and various fruits are cultivated throughout the entire year.
sentences.literal: This region mild being, one-year throughout various fruits cultivated are.
sentences.nuanceNote: Unbroken continuum throughout the full calendar year.

quiz.question: ボランティア活動（　　）、多くの素晴らしい仲間と出会うことができた。
quiz.translation: Through volunteer activities, I was able to meet many wonderful companions.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜を通じて intermediary medium
quiz.ruleHint: N + を通じて / を通して (つうじて / とおして)

explanations.reason: Correct! ボランティア活動を通じて means "by way of / through the experience of volunteer work".
Incorrect. にわたって measures numerical duration/expanse, not a qualitative medium.
Incorrect. にかけて requires starting and ending bounds (AからBにかけて).
Incorrect. に際して means "on the ceremonial occasion of".

title: 〜に限り（にかぎり） (Strictly limited to... exclusive privilege)
meaning: An exceptional privilege, special deal, or strict rule that applies ONLY and exclusively to this specific group or timeframe.
connection: N + に限り / に限る
nuance: に限り is common in formal restrictions. に限って can also restrict a case; additional uses express unlucky timing or confidence that a particular person would not do something. Context distinguishes these uses.
keyTakeaway: に限り is common in formal restrictions. に限って can also restrict a case; additional uses express unlucky timing or confidence that a particular person would not do something. Context distinguishes these uses.

sentences.japanese: 本日ご来店いただいたお客様に限り、全商品を２０％オフでご提供いたします。
sentences.english: Strictly limited to customers visiting our store today, we offer 20% off all products.
sentences.literal: Today store-visit received customers strictly-to-limited, all-products 20%-off at provide will.
sentences.nuanceNote: Special commercial privilege with strict temporal boundary.

tokens.reading: ごらいてんいただいた
おきゃくさまにかぎり
にじゅっぱーせんとオフで
ごていきょういたします

quiz.question: 本日（　　）限り、入場無料です。
quiz.translation: Admission is free today only.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜に限り exclusive promotional qualification
quiz.ruleHint: N + に限り / に限る

explanations.reason: に限り means limited to.
を限り is not the required form here.
で限り is not the required form.
が限り is not the required form.

title: 〜に限って（にかぎって） (Of all unlucky days! / Selective trust)
meaning: 1) Of all days/times, something inconvenient or unfortunate happens specifically on this occasion (Murphy's Law!). 2) Because I know X, that person of all people would never do such a thing.
connection: N + に限って
nuance: に限り is common in formal restrictions. に限って can also restrict a case; additional uses express unlucky timing or confidence that a particular person would not do something. Context distinguishes these uses.
keyTakeaway: に限り is common in formal restrictions. に限って can also restrict a case; additional uses express unlucky timing or confidence that a particular person would not do something. Context distinguishes these uses.

sentences.japanese: 傘を持ってこなかった日に限って、突然の大雨に見舞われる。
sentences.english: Of all days, it suddenly pours heavily on the exact day I didn't bring an umbrella.
sentences.literal: Umbrella brought-not day strictly-on, sudden heavy-rain struck-by.
sentences.nuanceNote: The universal frustration of Murphy's Law in daily life.

tokens.meaning: of all days / specifically on the day

quiz.question: 急いでいる時（　　）、前の車がやたらと遅くてイライラする。
quiz.translation: Of all times, specifically when I am in a hurry, the car in front is dreadfully slow and irritates me.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜に限って Murphy's Law frustration
quiz.ruleHint: N + に限って

explanations.reason: Correct! 急いでいる時に限って perfectly captures the ironic, irritating bad timing.
Incorrect. に限り is for objective rule eligibility (discounts, admission), not subjective frustration.
Incorrect. に反して means "contrary to expectations/wishes".
Incorrect. を通じて means "throughout or via".

title: 〜ばかりか / 〜のみならず (Not only X... but even Y!)
meaning: Not only does state X apply, but something even further, unexpected, or more extreme Y is also the case.
connection: Plain form (V / い形 / な形-な / N-である) + ばかりか | のみならず
nuance: Escalation marker: Clause B adds something beyond the baseline expectation (often with も or さえ). Nuance distinction: 〜ばかりか often emphasizes surprise or grievance, while 〜のみならず is formal/written Japanese suitable for essays and academic speeches.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [A] ばかりか / のみならず [B も / さえ]. Escalating addition.

sentences.japanese: 彼は日本語ばかりか、中国語や英語もネイティブ並みに流暢に話すことができる。
sentences.english: He can speak not only Japanese, but also Chinese and English as fluently as a native.
sentences.literal: He Japanese not-only, Chinese and English also native-level fluently speak can.
sentences.nuanceNote: Japanese was already impressive; adding two more languages escalates the admiration.

quiz.question: 今回の不祥事は会社の信用を失墜させた（　　）、巨額の損害賠償問題にまで発展した。
quiz.translation: This recent scandal not only caused the company to lose its credibility, but escalated into a massive damages issue.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜ばかりか escalating consequence addition
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form (V / い形 / な形-な / N-である) + ばかりか | のみならず

explanations.reason: Correct! V-た (失墜させた) + ばかりか sets up the escalation: "not only X, but even went so far as Y".
Incorrect. わりに means "considering the ratio/standard" and doesn't express additive escalation.
Incorrect. 反面 presents a balancing opposite facet (e.g. convenient, but dangerous).
Incorrect. Ungrammatical here; doesn't form the "not only X, but even Y" pair with にまで.

title: 〜のに vs 〜ても (Frustration / Expectation Clash vs Pure Concession)
meaning: 〜のに: Despite X being true, unexpected result Y occurred (carries emotional complaint, disappointment, or shock). 〜ても: Even if condition X holds true, Y will still be the outcome.
connection: 〜のに: Plain form + のに / な形 + なのに / N + なのに | 〜ても: V-て + も / い形-くても / な形/N + でも
nuance: のに contrasts a fact with an unexpected result, often with surprise or dissatisfaction. ても concedes a condition while keeping the conclusion. Distinguish the concessive のに from purpose expressions such as 読むのに便利だ.
keyTakeaway: のに contrasts a fact with an unexpected result, often with surprise or dissatisfaction. ても concedes a condition while keeping the conclusion. Distinguish the concessive のに from purpose expressions such as 読むのに便利だ.

sentences.japanese: 毎日あんなに一生懸命勉強したのに、試験に受からなかった。
sentences.english: Even though I studied so hard every day, I did not pass the exam.
sentences.literal: Every-day that-much whole-heartedly studied although, exam-to pass-did-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Deep sense of betrayal of effort and emotional frustration.

quiz.question: 薬を飲んだ（　　）、まだ頭が痛いです。
quiz.translation: Although I took medicine, my head still hurts.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜のに non-past state connection with ongoing condition
quiz.ruleHint: 〜のに: Plain form + のに / な形 + なのに / N + なのに | 〜ても: V-て + も / い形-くても / な形/N + でも

explanations.reason: のに contrasts taking medicine with the persisting pain.
のを would nominalize as an object, but no suitable predicate follows.
のが would nominalize as a subject, not link these clauses.
のと does not link this contrast.

title: 〜わりに（は） vs 〜にしては (Ratio Assessment vs Strict Criteria Defier)
meaning: Evaluating results against a standard. わりに: "Considering the cost/age/effort, surprisingly... (proportion ratio)". にしては: "For someone belonging to category X, surprisingly... (concrete standard)".
connection: 〜わりに: Plain form (V / い形 / な形-な / N-の) + わりに | 〜にしては: Plain form (V / い形 / な形 / N) + にしては (NO の/な!)
nuance: Notice connection: 70歳なのに元気だ → 70歳のわりに(は)元気だ (Ratio) vs 70歳にしては元気だ (Criteria). In にしては, you CANNOT put な or の with nouns (70歳にしては, NOT 70歳のにしては ❌). わりに can be used with generic concept words like 値段, 年齢, 努力.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Noun + の + わりに(は). Noun (bare) + にしては. Both mean "unexpectedly for that standard".

sentences.japanese: このレストランの料理は、値段のわりにはボリュームがあって美味しい。
sentences.english: Considering the inexpensive price, this restaurant's food has generous portions and tastes great.
sentences.literal: This restaurant's food, price's considering volume having delicious is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Great cost-performance ratio: low price contrasted with high quality/portion.

quiz.question: 初めて作った料理に（　　）は、よくできています。
quiz.translation: It is well made for a first attempt at cooking.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜にしては noun connection without particles
quiz.ruleHint: 〜わりに: Plain form (V / い形 / な形-な / N-の) + わりに | 〜にしては: Plain form (V / い形 / な形 / N) + にしては (NO の/な!)

explanations.reason: にしては is the required fixed form.
にしたは does not form this comparison.
にするは does not form this comparison.
にしは is incomplete.

title: 〜反面（はんめん） vs 〜一方（いっぽう）（で） (Opposite Face vs Dual Perspectives)
meaning: Highlighting two contrasting aspects of the same topic. 反面: "On the flip side (sharp light and dark contrast)". 一方で: "While simultaneously / on the other hand (balanced contrast)".
connection: Plain form (V / い形) + 反面 / 一方（で） | な形 + な/である + 反面 / 一方（で） | N + である + 反面 / 一方（で）
nuance: 反面 literally means "the opposite surface of a coin": convenient on the surface, but fraught with hidden peril on the other. 一方で can contrast two different trends occurring in parallel (e.g. "Urban populations are rising, while rural populations are shrinking").
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Plus feature] 反面 [Minus feature]. Two sides of the exact same coin.

sentences.japanese: 大都市での生活は刺激的で便利な反面、生活費が高くストレスも溜まりやすい。
sentences.english: While life in a big city is stimulating and convenient, on the flip side, the cost of living is high and stress easily accumulates.
sentences.literal: Big-city-in life stimulating and convenient flip-side, living-costs high stress also accumulate-easy.
sentences.nuanceNote: A classic dual-faceted portrait: the glamor of city life contrasted with its steep costs.

quiz.question: リモートワークは通勤の負担がない（　　）、オンとオフの切り替えが難しくなりがちだ。
quiz.translation: While remote work has no commute burden, on the flip side, switching between on and off mode tends to become difficult.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜反面 contrasting dual aspects of single reality
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form (V / い形) + 反面 / 一方（で） | な形 + な/である + 反面 / 一方（で） | N + である + 反面 / 一方（で）

explanations.reason: Correct! 反面 cleanly balances the positive facet (no commute) against the negative flip side.
Incorrect. あげく requires past tense (た) denoting the bitter end of an ordeal.
Incorrect. ばかりに means "simply because of one mistake, disaster struck".
Incorrect. 次第 indicates immediate future execution, not contrast.

title: 〜ものの / 〜とはいうものの (Although it is a fact that... still)
meaning: Conceding that clause A is an undeniable factual reality, but pointing out that clause B fails to develop as one would naturally expect.
connection: Plain form (V / い形 / な形-である / N-である) + ものの | な形 + なものの
nuance: Formal written concession: "It is true that X, but in reality Y." Unlike casual けれど, ものの carries a mature, reflective tone often used in formal writing, reviews, and business retrospectives.
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Undeniable Fact] + ものの + [Shortcoming / Hesitation].

sentences.japanese: 新しいパソコンを購入したものの、機能が多すぎてまだ使いこなせていない。
sentences.english: Although I purchased a new PC, it has too many functions and I haven't been able to master it yet.
sentences.literal: New PC purchased although, functions too-many still master-can-not.
sentences.nuanceNote: Acknowledges the purchase as a fact, but laments the struggle to actually master the tool.

quiz.question: 春とは（　　）ものの、朝晩はまだまだ厳しい寒さが続いている。
quiz.translation: Although it is called spring, severe cold still continues in the mornings and evenings.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜とはいうものの fixed concessive compound
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form (V / い形 / な形-である / N-である) + ものの | な形 + なものの

explanations.reason: Correct! 「〜とはいうものの」 is the established idiomatic concession pattern meaning "although it is termed X".
Incorrect. とはいって cannot take ものの in this way.
Incorrect. といえば means "speaking of which", not concession.
Incorrect. といったら expresses extreme degree (e.g. その美しさといったら).

title: 〜どころか / 〜どころではない (Far from X... actually extreme Y!)
meaning: 1) 〜どころか: Far from being X, the real situation is completely opposite or dramatically more extreme! 2) 〜どころではない: I am in absolutely NO position / state of mind to even think of doing X.
connection: Plain form / N + どころか | V-辞書形 / N + どころではない
nuance: Massive psychological contrast! "Did you pass? Pass?! Far from passing, I got the lowest score in the class!" (合格どころか、最下位だった). With どころではない, it stresses absolute impossibility due to overwhelm: "Vacation? With this deadline, I can't even think of vacation!"
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [A] どころか [予想外の極端なB]! Completely shatters assumption A.

sentences.japanese: 貯金が増えるどころか、毎月の赤字で借金が増える一方だ。
sentences.english: Far from savings increasing, with our monthly deficits, our debts just keep growing.
sentences.literal: Savings increase far-from, monthly deficit-by debt increase continuous-trend is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Shatters the optimistic assumption (savings) and reveals the painful reality (growing debt).

quiz.question: 来週のプレゼンの準備で徹夜続きで、週末に遊びに行く（　　）。
quiz.translation: Because I've been pulling all-nighters preparing for next week's presentation, going out to have fun this weekend is completely out of the question.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜どころではない out of the question / overwhelming circumstances
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form / N + どころか | V-辞書形 / N + どころではない

explanations.reason: Correct! 「〜どころではない」 conveys: "I am in no condition or position to even consider having fun!".
Incorrect. どころか requires a contrasting extreme follow-up clause (e.g. 遊びに行くどころか寝る時間もない).
Incorrect. 反面 presents a dual balancing aspect, not overwhelming impossibility.
Incorrect. Ungrammatical sentence ending here.

title: 〜はずだ vs 〜かもしれない (Logical Expectation vs Unverified Possibility)
meaning: はずだ: an expectation based on a reason. かもしれない: a possibility, without a fixed numerical probability.
connection: 〜はずだ: Plain form (V / い形) + はずだ / な形 + なはずだ / N + のはずだ | 〜かもしれない: Plain form (without だ) + かもしれない
nuance: Notice connection: With nouns, はず demands の (田中さんの職務のはずだ), whereas かもしれない attaches bare to nouns without だ (雨かもしれない, NOT 雨だかもしれない ❌). Furthermore, 〜はずがない means "there is no logical way that... (complete disbelief)".
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: Noun + [のはずだ]. Noun (bare) + [かもしれない] (no だ!).

sentences.japanese: 彼は日本に５年間も留学していたのだから、日本語がペラペラなはずだ。
sentences.english: Since he studied abroad in Japan for as long as five years, he should be fluent in Japanese.
sentences.literal: He Japan-in 5-years studied because, Japanese fluent-should-be.
sentences.nuanceNote: Solid deduction based on the logical premise of a 5-year stay in Japan.

quiz.question: 今日は休み（　　）はずです。
quiz.translation: It should be a day off today.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜はずだ noun connection with の
quiz.ruleHint: 〜はずだ: Plain form (V / い形) + はずだ / な形 + なはずだ / N + のはずだ | 〜かもしれない: Plain form (without だ) + かもしれない

explanations.reason: A noun connects to はず with の.
を does not modify はず.
に does not modify はず here.
で alone is not the required noun modifier.

title: The "Wake" Trio: わけだ vs わけがない vs わけではない
meaning: 1) 〜わけだ: Naturally so / That explains why! 2) 〜わけがない: There is absolutely NO WAY (logical impossibility)! 3) 〜わけではない: It doesn't necessarily mean that (partial negation).
connection: Plain form (V / い形 / な形-な / N-の/な) + わけだ / わけがない / わけではない
nuance: The ultimate Japanese logic pillar! わけ signifies the internal reason/logic of the universe. わけだ = "The puzzle pieces fit, now I understand why it's cold!" わけがない = "Such a thing defies all reason and reality!" わけではない = "Don't jump to conclusions; it's not that I hate it, I'm just full."
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: わけだ (That explains it!), わけがない (Impossible!), わけではない (Not necessarily so!).

sentences.japanese: エアコンが故障しているのか。部屋がこんなに蒸し暑いわけだ。
sentences.english: So the air conditioner is broken? That explains why the room is so sweltering hot!
sentences.literal: Air-conditioner broken is? Room this-much humid-hot natural-reason is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Aha-moment realization: discovering the broken AC explains the sweltering heat.

tokens.reading: こしょうしているのか

sentences.english: It isn't that I dislike Japanese food, but natto is the one thing I just can't stomach.
sentences.literal: Japanese-food dislike not-necessarily, natto only by-all-means weak-at is.
sentences.nuanceNote: Partial negation: softening the statement to prevent misunderstanding.

quiz.question: あんなに誠実な彼が、仲間のお金を盗む（　　）。絶対に誤解だ。
quiz.translation: There is absolutely no way that a man as sincere as him would steal his companions' money. It is definitely a misunderstanding.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜わけがない absolute logical impossibility
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form (V / い形 / な形-な / N-の/な) + わけだ / わけがない / わけではない

explanations.reason: Correct! 「〜わけがない」 asserts complete logical impossibility: "there is no way he would steal!".
Incorrect. わけだ would mean "that explains why he stole", directly contradicting his sincere reputation.
Incorrect. わけではない means "it doesn't necessarily mean...", which is too weak and contradicts "definitely a misunderstanding".
Incorrect. ものだ expresses general truths, nostalgias, or social norms.

title: 〜に違いない（にちがいない） (Must be / Strong subjective certainty)
meaning: The speaker feels overwhelmingly certain that something is true, based on intuitive conviction or compelling circumstantial evidence.
connection: Plain form (V / い形 / な形 / N) + に違いない (NO だ with な-adj or Nouns!)
nuance: に違いない expresses strong conviction based on the speaker's reasoning or evidence. はずだ foregrounds an expectation. に決まっている is another expression of certainty, not a contraction of に違いない.
keyTakeaway: に違いない expresses strong conviction based on the speaker's reasoning or evidence. はずだ foregrounds an expectation. に決まっている is another expression of certainty, not a contraction of に違いない.

sentences.japanese: 現場に彼の手袋が落ちていたのなら、犯人は彼に違いない。
sentences.english: If his glove was left dropped at the crime scene, the culprit must be him without a doubt.
sentences.literal: Scene-at his glove fallen-was if, culprit he must-be.
sentences.nuanceNote: Strong, unshakeable deduction from damning physical evidence.

tokens.meaning: must be him without a doubt

quiz.question: 朝から何も口にしていないのだから、彼は今とても（　　）に違いない。
quiz.translation: Since he hasn't eaten a single bite since morning, he must be extremely hungry right now without a doubt.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜に違いない connection with current continuous state
quiz.ruleHint: Plain form (V / い形 / な形 / N) + に違いない (NO だ with な-adj or Nouns!)

explanations.reason: Correct! V-ている form (お腹が空いている) + に違いない conveys "he must be hungry right now".
Incorrect. だろう cannot be nested inside に違いない.
Incorrect. Adding こと is redundant and ungrammatical here.
Incorrect. Negative form contradicts having eaten nothing all day.

title: 〜にほかならない (Is nothing other than... / Absolutely none other than)
meaning: Strongly and authoritatively declaring that X is the sole, definitive cause or essence of something: "It is nothing other than X."
connection: N + にほかならない | から + にほかならない (Because of none other than...)
nuance: Formal, assertive, and philosophical. Frequently appears in conclusion paragraphs of JLPT N2/N1 essays and editorial speeches: "This victory is due to nothing other than our team's unflagging efforts" (チームの努力の賜物にほかならない).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [Noun / 理由] + にほかならない = "It is definitively X and nothing else!"

sentences.japanese: 彼が今回の難関プロジェクトを成功させることができたのは、日頃の弛まぬ努力の結果にほかならない。
sentences.english: That he was able to make this formidable project a success is nothing other than the result of his constant daily efforts.
sentences.literal: He formidable project succeed-cause able-was that-which, daily unflagging effort result nothing-other-than.
sentences.nuanceNote: Categorical attribution of success solely to steadfast diligence.

quiz.question: これは努力の結果に（　　）。
quiz.translation: This is nothing other than the result of effort.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜からにほかならない reason attribution pattern
quiz.ruleHint: N + にほかならない | から + にほかならない (Because of none other than...)

explanations.reason: にほかならない completes the assertion.
The connective form does not finish this assertion.
