This is not a completed conjugation.

title: 〜っこない vs 〜かねない vs 〜かねる (Impossibility vs Danger vs Polite Hesitation)
meaning: 1) 〜っこない: No way in hell / absolutely impossible (spoken conviction). 2) 〜かねない: Might result in something terrible (grave danger). 3) 〜かねる: Hesitate / cannot bring myself to do (formal polite refusal).
connection: All attach to V-stem (ます形 without ます)! V-stem + っこない / かねない / かねる
nuance: THE TRIPLE JLPT N2 TRAP: Notice that 〜かねない ends in ない (negative appearance), but means POSITIVE DANGER ("it might very well happen!"). 〜かねる ends affirmative, but means CANNOT ("I am unable to accept"). 〜っこない is forceful conversational rejection ("I could never run a marathon!").
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: かねない = "Bad thing MIGHT happen!" かねる = "Politely cannot do." っこない = "No chance!"

sentences.japanese: こんな大雨の中でスピードを出しすぎると、大事故を起こしかねない。
sentences.english: If you speed in this heavy rain, you might very well cause a major accident.
sentences.literal: This heavy-rain inside speed excess-produce-if, major-accident cause-danger-exists.
sentences.nuanceNote: Warning about a severe, dangerous risk that could easily manifest.

tokens.meaning: if you exceed / produce too much

tokens.nuance: Stem 起こし + かねない

quiz.question: 申し訳ございませんが、個人情報に関わるお問い合わせにはお答えいたし（　　）。
quiz.translation: We are terribly sorry, but we cannot answer inquiries involving personal information.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜かねる polite business refusal
quiz.ruleHint: All attach to V-stem (ます形 without ます)! V-stem + っこない / かねない / かねる

explanations.reason: Correct! 「いたしかねます」 is the quintessential business Japanese phrase politely refusing an impossible request.
Incorrect. かねない means "there is a dangerous risk that we will answer", which is completely backwards.
Incorrect. っこない is casual/colloquial and highly rude in formal customer service.
Incorrect. すぎます means "doing excessively".

title: Giving & Receiving Triad: あげる vs くれる vs もらう (+ て-forms)
meaning: Tracking favors and social debt. 〜てあげる: I/insider do favor outward. 〜てくれる: Outside person kindly does favor inward to me. 〜てもらう: I humbly receive/benefit from another's favor.
connection: V-て + あげる / くれる / もらう (Humble: 差し上げる, いただく | Honorific: くださる)
nuance: Track the giver, receiver and subject. 先生が説明してくださった and 先生に説明していただいた describe the same favor from different grammatical viewpoints. Offering てあげる or even て差し上げる can sound presumptuous; a respectful offer need not explicitly describe a favor.
keyTakeaway: Track the giver, receiver and subject. 先生が説明してくださった and 先生に説明していただいた describe the same favor from different grammatical viewpoints. Offering てあげる or even て差し上げる can sound presumptuous; a respectful offer need not explicitly describe a favor.

table.title: Giving & Receiving Triad (授受動詞): あげる vs くれる vs もらう
table.subtitle: Tracks social perspective, insider/outsider psychology, and debt of gratitude.

rows.label: X は Y に あげる / 〜てあげる
cells: X (Giver / "I" or insider)
From Speaker/Insider OUTWARD to Receiver
差し上げる (さしあげる - Humble toward higher status)
CAUTION: Doing a favor directly to a superior with 〜てあげます can sound condescending. Avoid!
rows.note: Subject = Giver. Particle に = Receiver.

rows.label: X が 私に くれる / 〜てくれる
cells: X (Giver / Outside party)
From Outside party INWARD to Speaker / My In-Group
くださる (Honorific - Superior gave to me)
TRAP: The subject is ALWAYS the person who gives, and the recipient is ALWAYS "私" (or my family/in-group)!
rows.note: 先生が私に本をくださった (Teacher gave me a book).

rows.label: 私 は X に/から もらう / 〜てもらう
cells: 私 (Receiver / Beneficiary as Subject)
Speaker RECEIVES from Giver
いただく (Humble - I humbly received from superior)
TRAP: The subject is the RECEIVER! Marked by は. The source/giver is marked by に or から.
rows.note: 田中さんに手伝ってもらった (I got Tanaka-san to help me).

sentences.japanese: 雨で濡れていた私に、親切な見知らぬ人が傘を貸してくれた。
sentences.english: A kind stranger lent an umbrella to me, who was getting drenched in the rain.
sentences.literal: Rain-by drenched-was me-to, kind stranger umbrella lent-gave.
sentences.nuanceNote: The stranger is the actor/giver; the favor flowed inward to the grateful speaker (私に〜てくれた).

quiz.question: 日本語の文法が分からなかったので、田中先生に（　　）。
quiz.translation: Because I didn't understand Japanese grammar, I got Tanaka-sensei to explain it to me.
quiz.grammarFocus: 〜てもらう / いただく with subject as recipient
quiz.ruleHint: V-て + あげる / くれる / もらう (Humble: 差し上げる, いただく | Honorific: くださる)

explanations.reason: Correct! 「先生に説明していただいた」 (I humbly received an explanation from teacher) correctly matches the particle に marking the teacher.
Incorrect. If using くださった, the teacher must be the subject marked by が: 田中先生が説明してくださった.
Incorrect. あげた means YOU explained it to the teacher, which is arrogant and contextually upside down.
Incorrect. やった is condescending, used only for pets or watering plants.

title: The Voice Transformation Ladder: Passive (受身) → Causative (使役) → Causative-Passive (使役受身)
meaning: 1) 受身: Action received / Suffering passive (雨に降られた). 2) 使役: Make or let someone do (子供に野菜を食べさせる). 3) 使役受身: Forced to do against one's own will (無理やり酒を飲まされた).
connection: 受身: あ-stem + れる / られる | 使役: あ-stem + せる / させる | 使役受身: あ-stem + される (Contracted) / させられる
nuance: THE SUFFERING PASSIVE (迷惑受身): Japanese uses passive voice when someone suffers from an uncontrollable external event: 電車の中で足を踏まれた (someone stepped on my foot), 泥棒に財布を盗まれた (my wallet was stolen by a thief). In CAUSATIVE-PASSIVE (使役受身), you are forced to endure something: ３時間も立たされた (I was made to stand for 3 whole hours!).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: [あ-stem + される / させられる] = "I was forced to do it against my will!"

table.title: The Voice Transformation Matrix: Active → Passive → Causative → Causative-Passive
table.subtitle: From direct acts to being victimized (迷惑受身) to being coerced (使役受身).

rows.label: 受身 (Passive)
cells: Action received. Includes Suffering Passive (迷惑受身) where speaker is inconvenienced.
あ-stem + れる (書く → 書かれる, 踏む → 踏まれる)
Stem + られる (食べる → 食べられる, 褒める → 褒められる)
する → される / くる → こられる
rows.note: Suffering Passive: 雨に降られた (I was rained on / inconvenienced by rain).

rows.label: 使役 (Causative)
cells: Make / Let someone do something. Expresses authority, permission, or triggering emotion.
あ-stem + せる (行く → 行かせる, 読む → 読ませる)
Stem + させる (食べる → 食べさせる)
する → させる / くる → こさせる

rows.label: 使役受身 (Causative-Passive)

title: 〜てたまらない vs 〜てならない (Unbearable Physical Urge vs Spontaneous Deep Emotion)
meaning: 1) 〜てたまらない: So overwhelmingly intense I can't bear it (physical sensation / direct urge). 2) 〜てならない: Spontaneous, deep emotional or instinctive feeling rising from within.
connection: V-て / い形-くて / な形-で + たまらない / ならない / しょうがない
nuance: CONTRAST: 〜てたまらない is visceral and immediate: 喉が渇いてたまらない (I am dying of thirst!), 痛くてたまらない (It hurts unbearably!). 〜てならない is psychological and reflective: 彼の将来が心配でならない (I cannot help feeling profound anxiety about his future).
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: たまらない = Visceral / Physical ("Can't stand it!"). ならない = Deep spontaneous psychology.

title: 〜ざるを得ない（ざるをえない） (Have no choice but to do / Compelled by circumstance)

nuance: Heavy reluctance: "Against all personal desire, cold objective reality gives me zero alternative." CRITICAL IRREGULARITY: The verb する does NOT become しざるを得ない! It becomes せざるを得ない (sezaru o enai). Always tested on JLPT N2!

title: 〜一方だ / 〜ばかりだ (Steadily trending in one direction)
meaning: A change continues in one direction.
connection: V dictionary + 一方だ / ばかりだ
nuance: Use with a predicate that describes change, such as 増える, 減る or 悪くなる. It does not necessarily mean that the rate accelerates. 一方だ can describe favorable or unfavorable trends; ばかりだ often presents an unwelcome trend. Other constructions with 一方 or ばかり have other meanings, so do not apply this restriction to every occurrence of the word.
keyTakeaway: Continuing in one direction does not mean accelerating.

title: 〜をもとに vs 〜に基づいて (Creative Material vs Statutory / Fact Basis)
meaning: に基づいて: based on a foundation or grounds. をもとに: using something as a basis or material.
connection: Nに基づいて / Nに基づくN; Nをもとに / NをもとにしたN
nuance: に基づいて presents the basis for a decision, action or account, often evidence, rules, experience or principles. It is not limited to laws/science and does not guarantee literal compliance with every detail. をもとに can introduce source material used to develop something, such as an account or design. The meanings overlap; creative freedom versus strict compliance is a useful tendency, not an absolute boundary.
keyTakeaway: 基づく emphasizes grounds; をもとに emphasizes a source/basis. Context determines the contrast.

title: 〜に対して vs 〜にとって (Target / Contrast vs Personal Perspective)
meaning: 〜に対して: 1) Toward person/target (attitude/action). 2) In stark contrast to A, B is... 〜にとって: From the subjective perspective / standard of evaluating value for person X ("For me, this is important").
connection: N + に対して / に対する + N | N + にとって / にとっての + N
nuance: THE CLASSIC JLPT N3/N2 CONFUSION: Notice the direction! にとって evaluates psychological value or impact on the person ("To a child, play is education"). に対して directs an action or emotion outward toward an external target ("Be polite towards customers: お客様に対して丁寧にしなさい").
keyTakeaway: MUG-UP: にとって = "In my eyes / For me" (Value judgment). に対して = "Aimed toward target" OR "In contrast to".
